item.title: New York says no more subscriptions for in-car features—or does it?
item.description: Car buyers in New York may find the cost of ownership reduces a little next year. Maybe. Governor Kathy Hochul signed a bill yesterday that bans car companies and dealerships from locking up car features behind a subscription, a law that goes into effect on February 27 next year. “People spending their hard-earned money on a car shouldn’t have to fork over even more money for features that should automatically come with the car. My message to car companies is clear: this kind of deceptive business model isn’t going to fly in New York State. Keep your hands out of New Yorkers’ wallets,” the governor said. In the old days, the only options you paid to use after you bought a car were mods or upgrades you installed after the fact. That started to change with services like General Motors’ OnStar, which introduced telematics to the vehicle—for a monthly fee. Read full article Comments

item.title: Coldcard Postmortem Says Weak Seeds, Not Hacked Devices, Drove Bitcoin Thefts
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Coldcard Postmortem Says Weak Seeds, Not Hacked Devices, Drove Bitcoin Thefts Coinkite on Tuesday published its full postmortem on the Coldcard seed-generation flaw that let thieves drain bitcoin from customer wallets starting in July, saying no device was hacked and that the stolen keys were rebuilt offline from weak seeds. The 18-page report , dated Nov. 23 and modeled on a National Transportation Safety Board accident report, lays out how the defect shipped in Coldcard firmware from March 29, 2021, through July 30, 2026, and why years of outside reviews missed it. “The losses are real and, for some customers, life-changing. No report or firmware update can undo that. We are sorry,” Coinkite wrote. A silent swap in the random number generator A seed is the list of recovery words that controls a bitcoin wallet, and it is only as safe as the randomness used to create it. Coldcard devices were supposed to draw that randomness from the hardware random number generator built into their STM32 chip. Instead, a firmware setting switched that hardware source off, and a safeguard in Coinkite’s libNgU code library failed to catch it. Seed generation quietly fell back to Yasmarang, a predictable software generator built into MicroPython, the programming environment the firmware runs on. Nothing crashed, and the devices produced normal-looking seed words. Coinkite estimates affected seeds carried roughly 40 bits of effective security on the older Mk2 and Mk3 models and about 72 bits on the Mk4, Mk5 and Q, against an intended 128 bits. That shrinks the pool of possible seeds enough for attackers to search it offline. The report says Coinkite’s release checks confirmed the hardware code was present, but never confirmed that seed generation actually reached it. At least 15 independent review efforts since 2021 also missed the flaw, including two paid third-party reviews and an AI-assisted firmware review this year that produced 85 candidate findings. Hundreds of Coldcard owners report losses Unexpected transactions from affected seeds began July 29. Coinkite said it identified the defect the next day, after users discovered thefts, and shipped fixed firmware for every supported release track on July 31. As of Nov. 18, Coinkite had received about 300 loss-related support tickets tied to 242 customer accounts, or about 0.21% of its estimated Coldcard user base. The company’s blog post cites 236 accounts. Because Coldcard is self-custodial, Coinkite can only count losses that customers report, and it says the true number is likely higher. The report cites Galaxy Research figures showing 1,778.84 BTC stolen from more than 8,600 addresses, worth about $107 million at today’s price. Galaxy pegged losses above $115 million in August, based on prices when the coins were taken, and white hats later moved some exposed coins into a recovery trust. Who found and exploited the flaw is still unknown, and law enforcement is investigating. The report calls AI

item.title: Katsina suspends Emir of Daura’s engagements over assault allegation, launches investigation
item.description: By Fauziyya Lawal, Katsina The Katsina State Government has constituted an investigative committee to probe allegations of sexual assault involving the Emir of Daura, Alhaji Umar Faruk Umar, and a foreign tourist. The government also announced the suspension of the traditional ruler’s official engagements and travels pending the outcome of the investigation. The decisions were contained in a statement issued on Tuesday by the Commissioner for Information and Culture, Dr Bala Salisu Zango, on behalf of the state government. According to the statement, Governor Dikko Umaru Radda expressed serious concern over the allegations, describing the matter as one requiring careful attention and appropriate action. The governor consequently directed the immediate constitution of an investigative committee to examine the allegations and advise the government on the appropriate course of action. The statement said the decision was informed by the seriousness of the allegations and the need to establish the facts surrounding the reported incident. The government assured the public that justice would be served, adding that the findings and recommendations of the committee would be fully implemented. It said the suspension of the Emir’s official engagements and travels was among the measures taken by the government while the investigation lasted. The government also appealed to residents and members of the public to remain calm, law-abiding and refrain from actions capable of disrupting public peace. It urged residents to continue with their normal activities, reaffirming its commitment to handling the matter appropriately. The outcome of the committee’s investigation is expected to guide further action by the state government. The post Katsina suspends Emir of Daura’s engagements over assault allegation, launches investigation appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: New Xbox Was Originally Planned to Ditch Paid Multiplayer
item.description: All signs point to the next generation of console hardware being historically expensive. With rising component costs, the PS5 and Xbox Series are going for hundreds more than they did when they launched in 2020. In that context, it’s frightening to imagine the price of an even more powerful system, with one estimate placing potential manufacturing costs between $1,200 and $1,800 .

item.title: Man Utd win appeal over Yoro red card
item.description: Leny Yoro’s one-match suspension for the red card he was shown in Manchester United’s 4-0 mauling by Liverpool has been overturned, the Football Association announced on Tuesday. The French defender was dismissed in the eighth minute at Anfield for bringing down Alexander Isak as he advanced towards goal, with referee Sam Barrott deciding Yoro had denied an obvious goalscoring opportunity. United indicated on Monday that they intended to appeal for wrongful dismissal and a one-match suspension for the centre-back has now been lifted. The FA said the written reasons for their decision would be published in due course. Yoro, 21, will now be available for Saturday’s 1500 GMT kick-off against Brentford at Old Trafford. Dominik Szoboszlai scored Liverpool’s opening goal directly from the free-kick awarded for Yoro’s challenge and the home team cantered to an easy win. One question raised over the Yoro incident was whether Isak had the ball sufficiently under control for it to count as denial of an obvious goalscoring opportunity. United captain Bruno Fernandes told the BBC after the match that it was “never a red card”, adding: “I think it’s too many referees on the pitch and too many on VAR, seated, with such a long time to see and put it back, go forward, put it back, do it in slow motion, whatsoever. “To make a mistake like this can change a game. But obviously, then, it’s not because of them that we concede the goal from the free-kick, but it changes completely the flow of the game.” Mauricio Pochettino’s Manchester United tenure got off to the worst possible start at Anfield, with a defeat that keeps them in the Premier League relegation zone after just one top-flight win all season. The post Man Utd win appeal over Yoro red card appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: NAFDAC faults Edo committee over drug seizures, business closures
item.description: Seeks Okpebholo’s intervention over Arden Table Water By Chioma Obinna The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) has faulted the Edo State Consumer Protection Committee (ESCPC) over the alleged seizure of pharmaceutical products, closure of business premises and imposition of fines on operators without proper regulatory authorisation. The agency also appealed to Edo State Governor, Senator Monday Okpebholo, to intervene in the reported shutdown of Chepfets Mega Investment Nigeria Limited, manufacturer of Arden Table Water, insisting that the product’s registration was undergoing renewal and that this did not establish that it was unsafe or substandard. The Director-General of NAFDAC, Prof. Mojisola Adeyeye, raised the concerns while clarifying the agency’s position on the committee’s activities in the state. She expressed concern over reports that the committee had been using NAFDAC’s product authentication platforms to verify regulated products and make public declarations about their authenticity and quality. Adeyeye explained that access to the agency’s authentication platforms did not automatically confer regulatory authority on users or provide the technical basis for declaring products counterfeit, adulterated, injurious, safe or unsafe. NAFDAC said it recognised the importance of consumer protection and welcomed collaboration with state governments and other stakeholders in the fight against counterfeit, falsified, adulterated and substandard products. However, it stressed that such interventions must respect established regulatory boundaries and applicable laws. The agency said it was particularly concerned by reports that the committee had seized regulated products, publicly labelled some products fake or adulterated, sealed business premises and imposed fines on operators under the guise of working for NAFDAC without its authorisation or guidance. It also raised concerns over the reported deployment of NAFDAC’s Automated Product Administration and Monitoring System (NAPAMS), QR code scanner, Short Messaging Service (SMS) verification platform and other regulatory tools by the committee to assess products and make public pronouncements on their identity, authenticity, efficacy and effectiveness. According to the agency, failed QR code scans, missing registration details or inconsistencies in product packaging do not, on their own, constitute sufficient evidence that a product is counterfeit or substandard. It advised consumers and other stakeholders to report such irregularities to NAFDAC for investigation and possible laboratory analysis, urging the public to await the agency’s findings before making claims about products. On the reported enforcement activities, NAFDAC condemned what it described as the unilateral seizure of pharmaceutical products, closure of establishments and imposition of fines by the committee. item.title: Man Utd's Yoro has Anfield red card overturned
item.description: Leny Yoro was sent off for this tackle on Alexander Isak [Getty Images] Manchester United defender Leny Yoro has had the red card he was shown during Sunday's Premier League match at Liverpool overturned. The Football Association has confirmed Yoro will now be clear to face Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday. "Leny Yoro's one-match suspension has been removed following a successful claim of wrongful dismissal," said the FA in a statement. New United head coach Mauricio Pochettino was furious at the decision, which came just eight minutes in and, he felt, changed the course of the game, which Liverpool won 4-0. Liverpool striker Alexander Isak ran on to a ball that bounced over Matthijs de Ligt but took a heavy touch that meant the ball was likely to run through to United goalkeeper Senne Lammens even if Yoro had not brought the Swede down. Nevertheless, referee Sam Barrott sent Yoro off, drawing criticism from Pochettino. "The ball wasn't in his control," he said. "Isak, when he saw the control wasn't good, it's normal to delay, and stop to the run. In that moment that Yoro came from the back, and you go down. "But all that we play football; you know that wasn't intentional. That is never a foul." 'No-one's coming to save us' - but how can Man Utd save themselves? Sporting boss Fonseca dismisses Man Utd fragile talk United have travelled to Lisbon for their next Champions League match on Wednesday (20:00 GMT). The early dismissal of Yoro at Anfield meant Sporting had no chance to assess any changes Pochettino might have made after he replaced Michael Carrick during the international break. But despite United sitting 19th in the Premier League, Sporting boss refuses to accept United are "fragile". "I don't following the reasoning," said Fonseca, who was only appointed on 4 November after the Portuguese club bought him out of his contract at Lyon. "Manchester is a great team," he said. "I don't believe a lot that great teams are fragile. The last game they played in the Champions League, they were trailing 2-0, then won 3-2 against a very difficult opponent in Roma. "Moreover, when they have a new head coach, with such world-class players, it's extremely unpredictable to see if they will have a good day or bad day." United have not won in the Premier League since August and have conceded 19 goals in their past six games in all competitions. Yet, such was the nature of the Liverpool game, Fonseca has had to watch analysis of Pochettino's time in charge of the United States to get an idea of what to expect. "Eight minutes, red card. It's impossible to make an analysis," he said. "I tried to see Pochettino with the United States and what kind of solutions he used. There is some information but it is very difficult to predict." item.title: 'I could throw three interceptions... and not want to go hang myself': Troy Aikman remembers Tom Jackson, 'NFL Primetime'
item.description: Credit: 'Monday Night Countdown' Troy Aikman’s tribute to Tom Jackson on Monday night was warm, heartfelt, and about one word choice away from going off without a hitch. Aikman appeared on Monday Night Countdown ahead of Bengals-Commanders to eulogize Jackson, who died Friday at 75 , and dedicated most of his remembrance to the sacrosanct Sunday night ritual that bookended nearly every week of his Hall of Fame career in Dallas. The 60-year-old Aikman recalled that arriving home after a game and tuning in to NFL Primetime was the only way a player of his generation could take stock of everything that had unfolded across the league. And for a quarterback, the show was also the definitive barometer of how his afternoon compared with the rival passers he was constantly measuring himself against. “Him and Boomer, they were so good, you know, obviously great friends, great chemistry, but what I respected probably as much as anything about that show was they could be critical and opinionated, but they didn’t attack people,” Aikman said. “Like I could throw three interceptions in a game and we could lose and I could watch Primetime and not want to go hang myself at the end of the night. They just had a respectful way of presenting the information and letting everybody know what happened, but doing it the right way, I thought. And anyone who knew Tom knew that’s who he was.” Troy Aikman: “I could throw three interceptions in a game, and we could lose, and I could watch [NFL Primetime] and not want to go hang myself at the end of the night. They had a respectful way of presenting the information and letting everybody know what happened…” https://t.co/Fu3f0aiMpp — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 24, 2026 Beneath the clumsy wording, though, lay a sentiment that would resonate with anyone who spent Sunday nights in the late ’80s and ’90s waiting for Berman and Jackson to make sense of the afternoon. Primetime aired on Sunday nights from 1987 through 2005, a span that covered all 12 of Aikman’s seasons with the Cowboys; for most of that stretch, there was no RedZone, no streaming, and no highlight clipped and circulated online before the extra point sailed through the uprights. Berman supplied the nicknames and the bombast while Jackson, a 14-year Broncos linebacker who anchored the vaunted “Orange Crush” defense, gave viewers an authoritative account from a former player’s perspective. The show kept its stranglehold on Sunday nights until NBC locked up the extended highlight rights that came with Sunday Night Football . Berman broke the news himself on Sunday morning, opening Sunday NFL Countdown with an emotional tribute to the partner ESPN had once immortalized by naming its NFL studio after both men , and the program revived the beloved Jacked Up segment in Jackson’s memory. item.title: Could Aaron Donald play in 2027?
item.description: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - OCTOBER 25: Aaron Donald #99 of the Los Angeles Rams looks on in the second quarter of a game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) | Getty Images Could Aaron Donald really return to the NFL in 2027? After stepping away from football following the 2023 season, the former Los Angeles Rams defensive tackle has found himself back around the game in 2026, and the possibility of another season is worth hypothesizing. One of the biggest reasons a return could be appealing is that Donald appears to be having fun again. When he originally retired, it wasn’t necessarily because he had lost his love for football. Rather, the grind of an NFL season had taken its toll. Donald spent much of his career dealing with constant double and triple teams, making it increasingly difficult to enjoy the game when opposing offenses built their entire protection schemes around stopping him. “I think we’ve got a good core group, that played with each other, that knows how to play with each other.” 🎙️ Aaron Donald on the Defense pic.twitter.com/XtjotPMMco — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) November 22, 2026 That could make the idea of returning under different circumstances particularly interesting. For years, Donald was the player opposing offenses had to account for on every snap. Garrett has become one of the league’s most dominant defensive forces in his own right. Putting those two together has created a nightmare for opposing offensive lines. More importantly, Garrett gives Donald something he rarely experienced during his prime: another elite pass rusher demanding attention. Instead of facing constant double teams, Donald is now having opportunities to attack one-on-one matchups while Garrett draws his own share of protection. Next time we see get to the see the dynamic duo of Aaron Donald & Myles Garrett in action is on Thanksgiving Eve 👀 Rams captain @qlakee pulled back the curtain with @brock .vereen & @alex_curry on what it’s really like sharing a locker room with Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett.… pic.twitter.com/BG2wFYzI2t — 97.1 The Fan (@TheFanLA) November 21, 2026 At this stage of his career, Donald knows that he does not have to carry a defense. He gets to pick his spots, create pressure in obvious passing situations and make an impact without having to play every down. Of course, there are significant questions. Donald would be approaching another year away from his original retirement, and the physical demands of playing defensive tackle at the NFL level are enormous. Even for one of the greatest defensive players in league history, returning for 2027 would be a considerable challenge. Still, if Donald is enjoying football again and the opportunity to keep playing alongside Garrett is still available, it’s difficult to completely dismiss the possibility. item.title: Titans Hold No. 1 Draft Spot As Three Teams Sit At 1-9
item.description: Credit: Kirby Lee-USA TODAY Sports The Tennessee Titans still control the No. 1 spot in the 2027 NFL Draft despite a 51-30 loss to the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday. The franchise fell to 1-9 on the season, but they kept the top pick because of their weaker schedule compared to the other bad teams. The Los Angeles Chargers and Miami Dolphins also dropped to 1-9 records after their own losses, creating a three-way tie at the bottom of the league standings. According to a report , the Titans overtook the Chargers for the top spot last week after Los Angeles finally won a game, but the Chargers lost again on Sunday to the New York Jets. Now the race for the first overall selection is down to just these three clubs, and the tiebreaker rules will decide who gets the prize. Tiebreakers Favor Tennessee and Los Angeles Miami sits at third place in this race because the Dolphins face the toughest schedule of the three teams. According to reports, the Dolphins’ opponents have a .595 winning percentage, which is higher than the Titans’ .483 and the Chargers’ .531. This math means Miami needs to lose more games than the other two teams just to climb above them in the draft order. The Dolphins lost 26-9 to the Buffalo Bills on Sunday, marking their fourth straight defeat in a row. The team has been outscored 93-59 during this losing skid, and the offense has averaged under 15 points a game. Kyle Crabbs, who covers the Dolphins for Yahoo Sports, noted that the front office is not panicking despite the 1-8 start because everyone knew the roster was in a tough spot. The Quarterback Question Looms Large With the offense struggling, the need for a new quarterback has become the main topic for the Miami front office. Crabbs admitted he does not love any of the current quarterback prospects in the 2027 class. “I have a hard time falling in love with any of these guys,” Crabbs said. He listed Oklahoma State’s Drew Mestemaker, Notre Dame’s CJ Carr, and Miami’s Darien Mensah as names in play, but he feels the raw production does not reflect how Malik Willis has actually played. Willis is under contract for two more seasons, which gives the team a bridge to develop a rookie without rushing him onto the field. A Week 16 Showdown Could Decide It All A matchup at Hard Rock Stadium in Week 16 between the Chargers and Dolphins could decide which squad ends up with the poorest record. Both clubs face huge draft ramifications from that matchup as they try to secure the top pick. Miami hosts the Jets this week on Sunday, Nov. 29, before a long road trip that includes stops in Denver and Green Bay. The Dolphins have seven games left in the regular season, and two matchups against the Jets and Chargers look very winnable for the home team. Losing to the Chargers during Week 16 would improve Miami’s standing relative to one of the two teams currently tied with them. item.title: NASA may get $2 billion boost as White House seeks to accelerate Artemis
item.description: As part of ongoing wrangling over the US budget for the current fiscal year, the White House on Monday night sent a list of budget exceptions to Congress it seeks in the near-term for the federal government ( see .pdf ). The list of so-called "funding anomalies" is dominated largely by appropriations for the Department of Defense, including the Golden Dome missile defense program championed by the Trump administration. However, among the highest non-defense exceptions is $2 billion for NASA's Artemis program for a "higher rate of operations." The funding represents a significant 25 percent boost for NASA's Artemis program, which received approximately $7.8 billion in fiscal year 2026. Technically, the White House is seeking to increase the annualized funding rate for Artemis to $9.8 billion, rather than immediately providing NASA with an additional $2 billion. It comes at a time when it is increasingly clear that China's lunar ambitions are as expansive as those of NASA, and there is a very good chance the Asian country reaches the Moon with astronauts before NASA can get back there. item.title: Senegal reinstated as Afcon 2025 winners by court ruling
item.description: Sadio Mane's Senegal have been confirmed as Afcon 2025 winners following their appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport, giving the Teranga Lions a second continental title [Getty Images] Senegal have been reinstated as winners of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations after a ruling by the Court of Arbitration for Sport. The court's award overturns a previous decision which had stripped the West Africans of the title they won on the pitch during a chaotic final against host nation Morocco in January. The result of that match in Rabat, which saw the Teranga Lions triumph 1-0 after extra time, was overturned almost two months later when a Confederation of African Football (Caf) appeals board decreed Senegal had breached competition regulations by leaving the field of play in second-half stoppage time in protest at a penalty awarded against them. Senegal's football federation (FSF) subsequently appealed to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas), sport's highest legal authority, with a three-man panel hearing its case behind closed doors in Lausanne on 8 October. In a unanimous verdict, the Cas panel has effectively backed the decision by referee Jean-Jacques Ndala to restart the game after Senegal returned to the field and the match was played to a conclusion. The result of the final stands and Senegal are now confirmed as Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) 2025 winners. A statement issued by Cas said the court considered that "the referee's decision to resume the match or to stop it fell definitively within his sole authority". "By blowing his whistle to restart play, the referee considered that the conditions for resuming the match had been met - both teams were on the pitch again, and both expressed their willingness to resume." The FSF immediately reacted with a social media post featuring a picture of the side lifting the trophy in January captioned with the phrase "again and always champions of Africa". "The FSF welcomes this ruling with deep satisfaction," it later said in a statement. "This decision affirms, above all, the triumph of sporting fairness and reaffirms a fundamental principle: the true outcome of a match is determined exclusively on the field of play, under the protection of sports law." Meanwhile, Morocco's football federation (FRMF) expressed "surprise" at the ruling and added that it would "pursue all available legal avenues to challenge the decision". Caf is yet to comment but its president Patrice Motsepe has repeatedly said that his organisation will respect and adhere to the Cas ruling. The full grounds for the decision will be published by Cas in due course unless the parties request confidentiality. item.title: Hackensack-Teaneck Thanksgiving football game rescheduled due to storm
item.description: Another piece of North Jersey’s fading Thanksgiving football tradition is being pushed off the holiday this year, this time by the weather. The annual rivalry game between Hackensack and Teaneck, a Thanksgiving fixture dating to 1931, has been moved to Wednesday evening as a coastal storm threatens the region with heavy rain and strong winds. Kickoff is now scheduled for 6 p.m. at Teaneck High School. The change leaves one of North Jersey’s longest-running holiday rivalries without its traditional Thanksgiving morning setting. The other remaining Thanksgiving Day game, between Tenafly and Dumont, was also moved to Wednesday night because of the forecast. Story continues below photo gallery. The game was originally scheduled for Thanksgiving morning at 10:30 a.m. Kick-off will now be 6 p.m. Wednesday, Nov. 25, at Teaneck High School. “This decision was made with the safety and well-being of our student-athletes, twirlers, marching band, cheerleading teams, families, and community members as our top priority,” the Teaneck School District wrote in a statement. “We appreciate the understanding and flexibility of our students, families, alumni, and community members as we make this adjustment.” Ed Klimek, Teaneck's athletic director, said the main reason behind the decision was to allow the band, flag twirlers and cheerleaders, who had been practicing for weeks, to be able to perform. "Two years ago we played in an absolute monsoon," he said. "We can play football in the rain, but they can't perform in the rain. When I proposed this to Hackensack and to the football teams, everyone was on board." The parade to the field before the game, with the two teams’ school bands, cheerleaders and flag twirlers marching, is canceled, Klimek said. The traditional Thanksgiving Day team between the neighboring communities is one of the last played in North Jersey on the holiday. Many high school football teams have done away with the tradition of playing on Thanksgiving over the years, because of difficulties with the schedule and concerns that it would interfere with teams’ preparations for playing in championship games. The other remaining game scheduled for Thanksgiving Day between Tenafly and Dumont was also rescheduled to 6 p.m. Wednesday and will be played at Geissinger Field in Tenafly. The annual Thanksgiving Day rivalry game between Hackensack Comets and Teaneck Highwaymen dates back to 1931. Teaneck’s record for the season is 7-3. Hackensack is 4-4. Hackensack has dominated the matchup in recent years and has won the past 12 meetings between the two. This article originally appeared on NorthJersey.com: Hackensack-Teaneck Thanksgiving football game rescheduled due to storm

item.title: Chris Johnson responds to uncalled Josh Allen unsportsmanlike penalty
item.description: Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen certainly could have been called for unsportsmanlike conduct in a recent defeat of the Miami Dolphins , but wasn't. Dolphins rookie cornerback Chris Johnson and Allen were pushing and shoving at the end of an interception return by Jacob Rodriguez . Johnson was blocking Allen near a sideline when Allen appeared to fling him to ground by a facemask. Allen then shoved Johnson again when they are out of bounds. Was it a simple football play? Or should it have been a 15-yard penalty? Johnson said: "I saw J-Rod get the pick and from there on, I'm looking for a block. It just happened to be Josh Allen. I guess he didn't appreciate it much. And then we got tied up a bit." Johnson said he was surprised no flag was thrown. "Once you get into another players' helmet it's usually a flag," Johnson said. There was no broadcast replay, so here is #Bills Josh Allen’s scrap/fighting against #Dolphins corner Chris Johnson after his first interception via the All-22. #BillsMafia @BuffTrenchTalk pic.twitter.com/5txJ85EpiA — Carson Hayek (@CarsonHayek) November 23, 2026 Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley thought it was a penalty. "I saw it and our guys saw it because they were upset and then they started to talk and I said, I'll handle it," Hafley said. "And then I asked the refs. I'm not going to get into sending it to the league and everything that happened. I just, I don't understand how that is not a penalty. "And that is where I do have a hard time with that. Whatever you want to call happened, to me, that warranted a penalty. And it should have been 15 yards and the ball should have been moved up. So it happened, it's over, it was missed and we'll move on." Allen passed for 304 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions in a 26-9 victory. Allen did not have a single rushing attempt. This was likely intentional as the Bills have a game against the Chiefs on Thanksgiving. Allen, apparently, was focused on preserving his energy and health for the Kansas City game. The Dolphins will host the Bills in their penultimate game of the season on Sunday, January 3. Overreaction Monday: Time for Dolphins to move Kadyn Proctor to offensive tackle? item.title: NFL Mock Draft 2027: Eagles 7-round simulation, Version 2.0
item.description: SEATTLE, WA - NOVEMBER 21: Charlie Becker #80 of the Indiana Hoosiers warms up before a game between the Indiana Hoosiers and Washington Huskies on November 21, 2026 at Husky Stadium in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Henry Rodenburg/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Eagles notched their first win in two months on Sunday. However, the game didn’t give much hope to the prospect of actually turning the season around. Unless they beat Dallas on Thursday, Philly is a team that should be looking ahead to the 2027 NFL Draft. Due to their win and Jacksonville’s loss, the Eagles currently own the ninth and 24th pick in the first round. Right now, the biggest determinants of the Eagles’ draft strategy has to do with what is happening at quarterback and head coach. There are many factors that would lead to the Eagles not needing to draft a quarterback, but I am curious what that draft may look like if the position is taken care of ahead of the draft without sacrificing picks… IE, Jalen Hurts returns from his blood clots. Using the PFF Mock Draft Simulator with their draft board and not making any trades. 1.09: Charlie Becker, Wide Receiver, Indiana: Charlie Becker is a menace. Becker has 11 touchdowns through the air, 1,100 yards receiving, is averaging nearly 16 yards a catch and has yet to drop a ball this season. The 6’4”, 207 pound receiver is a physical, athletic deep threat who is able to use his long arms to win at the catch point and his long strides to pull away from defenses. The Eagles lack a true X-Receiver right now and Becker would immediately make the receiver position in Philadelphia a strength. Trevor Lauck, Offensive Tackle, Iowa: The Eagles need a youth movement on their offensive line. Trevor Lauck is a phenomenal prospect at left tackle, and would likely slide over to the right side to take over for Lane Johnson. He’d be a day one starter and day one difference maker. Boubacar Traore, Edge Defender, Notre Dame: The Eagles edge defender situation is bleak. Their best player right now is Nolan Smith, who may not even be with the team by the time the draft rolls around. Boubacar Traore is a bit leaner, but makes up for it with great length, burst, and a high motor. He is a tremendous pass rusher and has shown a lot as a run defender this season. Traore makes a ton of sense in the second round as someone who can really give a boost to this defense. Isaac Brown, Running Back, Louisville: The 2027 Eagles have been struggling in all phases of offense, but injuries have made their running game borderline unwatchable. Save for some big Saquon Barkley runs, they just don’t have quality depth at the running back position to move the ball in a meaningful way on the ground. Isaac Brown is a smaller running back prospect, but he is tremendous when he can get on the field. He has great vision, burst, and runs with a lot of grit. While he may not be an immediate every down back, there is a lot he can bring to the

item.title: Matthew McConaughey riding high after Commanders’ thrilling Bengals upset on MNF
item.description: Amber Searls-Imagn Images. Matthew McConaughey riding high after Commanders’ thrilling Bengals upset on MNF appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . After his Washington Commanders upset the Cincinnati Bengals on Monday Night Football (MNF), superfan Matthew McConaughey was feeling good. He took to X, formerly Twitter, to celebrate the win . The Oscar-winning actor appears to be feeling good about the Washington’s chances in the division, writing, “don’t look now but COMMANDERS comin ON!!! since ‘73. HAIL!!” The Commanders pulled off an upset against the Bengals in Week 11. It came down to the wire, as Drew Stevens kicked a game-winning field goal as time expired. He made all five of his field goal attempts on Monday night. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Joe Burrow was balling all night, passing for 300 yards and two touchdowns. However, the Bengals could not run the ball, only logging 31 yards on 14 carries. He almost threw an interception and took a big sack, leading to Evan McPherson’s second field goal with 46 seconds left. That was still too much time for Jayden Daniels, who led the Commanders into field goal range in four plays. He set Stevens up for a chip-shot 26-yard field goal that he made as time expired. This was a shocking win, especially given how well the Bengals had been playing coming into the game. They had won five games in a row after starting the season 2-2. They will have a chance to rebound in Week 12 when they play the New Orleans Saints. The Bengals will then play the Cleveland Browns before hosting the Kansas City Chiefs. The Commanders have won two games in a row and are in second place in the NFC East with a 4-5-1 record. They have only won their last two games by five points, but a win is a win. Their next game against a team with a record above .500 is in Week 16 when they play the Minnesota Vikings. Their next four opponents are the Arizona Cardinals (3-8), the Tennessee Titans (1-9), the Houston Texans (4-6), and the Atlanta Falcons (3-7). The 2025 All-Star heads to one of the best pitching organizations in baseball on a big one-year number. The deal is notable not only because of Bubic’s All-Star status, but also because of the financial commitment. A $17.5 million salary for a single season represents a significant investment, suggesting Cleveland sees an opportunity to add immediate value to its pitching staff without committing to a long-term contract. Cleveland adds another arm to its pitching staff Oct 12, 2026; Milwaukee, Wisconsin, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Kris Bubic (40) throws a pitch against the Milwaukee Brewers during the fifth inning in game two of the NLCS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at American Family Field. A one-year agreement also gives Bubic an opportunity to establish his value heading into the next free-agent cycle. Meanwhile, Cleveland gets an All-Star-caliber pitcher without taking on the risk of a multi-year commitment. The Guardians are clearly looking to strengthen their pitching staff, and adding Bubic represents an important early move in their offseason plans. item.title: Women’s Basketball: No. 15 TCU blows out Utah State, enters Thanksgiving undefeated
item.description: The No. 15-ranked TCU women’s basketball team turned in one of the best defensive performances in program history on Sunday. Jadyn Wooten led the Horned Frogs with 20 points, seven assists and seven rebounds as TCU held Utah State to eight first-half points in an 85-26 victory. The 26 points allowed are third fewest in history. Got an early start on Feast Week 🍗 #GoFrogs pic.twitter.com/NJBapDRw06 — TCU Women’s Basketball (@tcuwbb) November 23, 2026 Jessie-May Hall (13 points, seven rebounds and five assists) helped pace the offense and Lara Somfai (10 points, 11 rebounds) added a double-double for the Horned Frogs, who shot 51.2% from the floor and 40% from 3-point range in the win. Clara Silva (10 points, five rebounds, three steals) and Bella Hines (five points, three rebounds, two steals) rounded out the starting lineup. TCU forced 18 turnovers and held Utah State to 18.9% shooting. Third of the year, 10th of her career 🤝 #GoFrogs | @lara_somfai pic.twitter.com/VLOkeld3yx — TCU Women’s Basketball (@tcuwbb) November 23, 2026 Clara Bielefeld (eight points, four rebounds, four assists) and Camille Williams (eight points, two steals) led the bench unit. Sarah Portlock (four points, six rebounds), Claudia Contell (four points) and Avery Hjelmstad (three points) also contributed for the Horned Frogs, who had 58 points in the paint and 20 points off turnovers.

item.title: Senegal re-crowned Afcon champions after appeal upheld
item.description: Senegal have been re-crowned the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations champions after the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas) unanimously upheld their appeal against the decision to strip them of their title on Tuesday. Senegal contested Confederation of African Football's (Caf) decision to declare Morocco champions , wiping the Teranga Lions’ title from the records despite winning January’s Afcon final 1-0 after extra time in Rabat. The final was fraught with controversy after Senegal staged a walk-off in protest to a penalty was awarded against them in the dying stages of normal time, with players ordered into the dressing room by manager Pape Thiaw , where they remained for 14 minutes. Play was eventually resumed before Morocco’s Brahim Diaz missed the spot-kick, sailing a tame ‘Panenka’ effort into the arms of Edouard Mendy. Senegal went on to win the match in extra time through Pape Gueye. Brahim Diaz missed the penalty after Senegal staged a 14-minute walk-off (AFP/Getty) However, they were stripped of the title two months later after Caf’s Appeal Board ruled that Senegal had forfeited ⁠the match by walking off the pitch, overturning the result and awarding a 3-0 ​victory to ⁠Morocco. Senegal quickly followed with an appeal to sport's highest court, Cas, which was lodged on 25 March and have now successfully fought their case to be reinstated as champions, with the original 1-0 result restored. The three-man Cas ‌panel, presided over by French sports law ​expert Gerald Simon with assistance from ‌Italian international law professor ⁠Luigi Fumagalli and Hamburg-based ⁠attorney Ulrich Haas, ‌unanimously found that referee Jean-Jacques Ndala “did not commit any error of law”, said Cas secretary general Matthieu Reeb. Ndala’s decision to resume the match after Senegal’s walk-off fell within his sole authority and was therefore covered by the “field of play” doctrine, something Morocco’s federation argued was not the case. The court published its reasoning in a press release issued on Tuesday afternoon, which read: “By blowing his whistle to restart play, the referee considered that the conditions for resuming the match had been met – both teams were on the pitch again, and both expressed their willingness to resume. “In the panel’s view, there is no doubt that the effects of the referee’s decision were limited to the pitch.” The panel clarified that Articles 82 and 84 of Caf’s tournament regulations, cited in the Moroccan federation’s appeal, apply only to determining match results if team conduct forces a referee to permanently call off a game, and were therefore not applicable in this instance. "In conclusion, the panel considers that in resuming the match, the referee did not err in law," a court press release added. The Cas panel found referee Jean-Jacques Ndala did not commit any error when he allowed the match to continue (AFP via Getty Images) “The panel acknowledged that the referee had to make a decision in an atmosphere of extreme tension. item.title: Ajaokuta must work again, Kogi won’t be neglected – Atiku
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has pledged to revive the Ajaokuta Steel Mill, develop Idah River Port and complete the Kabba-Egbe road, promising to address longstanding infrastructure challenges across Kogi State. Speaking at his campaign rally in Lokoja, Atiku outlined development projects for the state’s three senatorial districts, including improved roads and water supply in Kogi East. He said the plans were aimed at creating jobs, expanding economic opportunities and making life more affordable for residents. According to the Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku said his proposed interventions would focus on turning the state’s economic potential into tangible benefits for its people. Addressing residents of Kogi East, he pledged to improve rural infrastructure and develop Idah River Port to ease the movement of agricultural produce and expand business opportunities. “To my brothers and sisters in Kogi East, I know what it means when a farmer cannot get produce to market because the road has failed, or when a family must struggle every day for clean water. We will improve your roads and water supply, and develop Idah River Port so that the region’s farmers and businesses can reach more customers,” he said. For Kogi Central, Atiku promised to revive the Ajaokuta Steel Mill, with a focus on restoring industrial production and creating employment. “Ajaokuta must finally become a working steel mill. I want its furnaces working, its gates open to skilled workers and its promise felt in the homes of the people who have waited so long. We will also support the roads and services that allow surrounding communities to benefit from that industry,” he said. In Kogi West, he pledged to complete the Kabba-Egbe road, which he said should no longer remain an unfulfilled promise. “The Kabba to Egbe road cannot remain an endless promise. We will complete it and make travel and trade easier for the communities along its route,” he stated. At the national level, Atiku also pledged to pursue the dredging of Baro Port and restore a targeted subsidy on fuel refined in Nigeria, saying the measures would help reduce transportation and production costs. The proposals formed part of his broader promise to translate infrastructure development and the state’s economic resources into employment and improved living conditions. item.title: Senegal’s AFCON Triumph Restored: Why It’s The Right Verdict
item.description: TOPSHOT - Senegal players celebrate with the trophy after winning the Africa Cup of Nations (CAN) final football match against Morocco at the Prince Moulay Abdellah Stadium in Rabat on January 18, 2026. (Photo by FRANCK FIFE / AFP via Getty Images) AFP via Getty Images The Court of Arbitration for Sport finally brought an end on Tuesday to one of the most extraordinary controversies in African soccer , restoring Senegal as champions of the Africa Cup of Nations and overturning a decision that threatened to undermine the authority of the game’s own rules. Nearly a year after that chaotic final in Morocco, Senegal can again celebrate its victory. The CAS ruling is not simply a triumph for the Senegal’s national team. It is also an important affirmation of the principles that should govern the sport: The authority of the match referee, the integrity of the result and the distinction between disciplinary regulations and decisions made during a game. The final was undoubtedly controversial. Senegal defeated Morocco 1-0 after extra time, but the game was overshadowed by a dramatic incident in second-half stoppage time. With the game still scoreless, Morocco was awarded a penalty kick. Senegal’s players protested the decision by leaving the field, resulting in a 15-minute delay. Congolese referee Jean-Jacques Ndala eventually allowed the game to resume. Morocco’s Brahim Diaz subsequently missed the penalty, then Senegal went on to score the decisive goal in extra time and win the game. There was little doubt that Senegal’s walk-off was an unacceptable response to a referee’s decision. Players cannot abandon a match because they disagree with a call. The tournament’s own regulations also provided for a team that refuses to play or leaves the field without the referee’s permission to forfeit the contest. The central question was never whether Senegal’s conduct deserved scrutiny. It was whether the circumstances justified overturning a completed match and later awarding Morocco a 3-0 victory by default. The Confederation of African Football’s appeals panel thought so when it ruled in March that Senegal had forfeited the Jan. 18 final. CAS has now correctly rejected that interpretation. The distinction is crucial. Tournament regulations exist to establish order, protect competition integrity and provide sanctions when teams refuse to fulfill their obligations. But those provisions must be interpreted within the broader framework of the game’s laws and the authority entrusted to referees. Referee decisions vs. tournament rules CAS determined that the relevant tournament regulations applied when a team’s conduct caused the referee to abandon a match permanently. That was not what happened in the Senegal-Morocco final. Ndala restarted the game. Senegal’s players returned to the field and indicated their willingness to continue. item.title: Jermod McCoy takes major leap
item.description: (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2026 draft class (eight of the 10 picks are on the 53-man roster) fared in a 38-24 road loss at the Denver Broncos on Sunday and what to look for Sunday at the Cleveland Browns: Fernando Mendoza: The No. 1 overall pick made his second career start. item.title: Barca have quality to win without Yamal: De Jong
item.description: Barcelona will be without winger Lamine Yamal for the match at Sabah but Frenkie de Jong says the team have the quality to win without him (Igor IVANKO) Barcelona midfielder Frenkie de Jong backed his team to continue their strong start to the Champions League on Wednesday at Sabah without injured star winger Lamine Yamal. The 19-year-old did not travel to Azerbaijan because of an ankle problem he sustained at the weekend. Barca have sometimes struggled without Yamal but De Jong said there was enough quality in the squad to prevail without the Spanish World Cup winner. "Having a player like Lamine missing, you'll always notice. He's a player with extraordinary talent, he makes danger by himself," De Jong told reporters Tuesday. "In a move without danger he can create it. You're going to feel that, but we have a squad filled with talent and very good players, so we're capable of winning tomorrow without him." Barca coach Hansi Flick agreed with the Dutch midfielder, but demanded focus from his side for the clash against Sabah. "We also played in the past without Lamine so we know what to do," said the coach. "For us he's a very important player, yesterday morning we checked him and decided it's better he stays at home. "Hopefully everything works well and he's available for the weekend." Flick said he had not decided who would line up in Yamal's spot, with Raphinha and Karim Adeyemi the most likely options. Barca's coach pointed out that Sabah, playing in the Champions League for the first time in their history, would be out to cause an upset against the five-time winners. "This is the first time in Sabah's history they are playing in the Champions League," noted the German. "They love playing in the Champions League against Barca and Manchester United. Every player is 100 percent motivated from them. "We need the same attitude and mentality from our players tomorrow." Sabah beat Slavia Prague in October for their first and only Champions League victory, while losing against Man United, Borussia Dortmund and Viking. bur-rbs/iwd

item.title: UAlbany's Tom Perkovich named finalist for FCS Coach of the Year
item.description: UAlbany new head coach Tom Perkovich during a summer practice on Thursday, July 30, 2026, at Casey Stadium in Albany, NY. (Jim Franco/Times Union) (Jim Franco/Times Union) University at Albany football coach Tom Perkovich, making the jump from Division III, led the Great Danes' turnaround to a Football Championship Subdivision playoff berth in his first season. For that accomplishment, Perkovich was named Tuesday as a finalist for the Eddie Robinson Award, given to the Football Championship Subdivision Coach of the Year, Perkovich is one of 15 finalists for the award, named after the late College Football Hall of Fame coach who guided Grambling for 55 seasons and won 408 games. UAlbany hired Perkovich last December after a successful decade at Division III Susquehanna University to take over a program that went 2-10 last season. The Great Danes improved to 8-4 under him, including 6-2 in the Coastal Athletic Association. They received an at-large bid to the FCS playoffs and will face Lehigh in a first-round game at noon Saturday in Bethlehem, Pa. "We put together a really good season and really happy we're in," Perkovich said. "We're excited for the opportunity and we'll be ready to play on the weekend at Lehigh. Really excited for our kids, our people on our campus, our alumni, everyone involved in our program. Just an amazing opportunity for us to play in the playoffs." The Great Danes were picked 11th in the CAA preseason coaches' poll. UAlbany has never won the Eddie Robinson Award, though Greg Gattuso was runner-up while guiding the Great Danes to the FCS semifinals for the first time in 2023. Other finalists for this year's award include a pair of former UAlbany assistant coaches, Lamar's Pete Rossomando and Western Illinois' Joe Davis. Monmouth coach Jeff Gallo, whose team won the Coastal Athletic Association with an undefeated league record and beat UAlbany, is also a finalist. All 13 FCS conferences are represented by a finalist. The winner, to be selected by a national voting panel, will be announced on Dec. 17 during a Stats Perform FCS National Awards Show on YouTube. Subscribe There’s more to Albany with the Times Union. Subscribe today for just 25¢. This article originally published at UAlbany's Tom Perkovich named finalist for FCS Coach of the Year .

item.title: Bundesliga planning new Saturday night kick-off time from 2029/30
item.description: Bundesliga planning new Saturday night kick-off time from 2029/30 The Bundesliga could introduce a new Saturday evening kick-off time from the 2029/30 season as part of the next domestic television rights cycle. According to Bild, plans are being drawn up to stage five marquee Bundesliga fixtures per season at 20:30 CET on Saturday evenings. The proposal was reportedly well received at a meeting of the 36 Bundesliga and 2. Bundesliga clubs in Frankfurt at the beginning of October, with the prospect of attracting larger television audiences in a prime-time slot appealing to potential broadcasters. Crucially, the traditional Saturday 15:30 kick-off time would remain unaffected, as would the existing 18:30 slot. Instead, four fixtures that would ordinarily take place at 19:30 on Sunday evenings would be moved to the new Saturday night slot. The fifth fixture would come from the Friday evening slot on the Easter weekend, with Bundesliga matches not taking place on Good Friday. The proposed changes would coincide with the start of the next domestic broadcasting rights cycle in the summer of 2029.

item.title: Penguins Practice: Malkin, Rust (Non-Contact) Participate
item.description: Injured forwards Evgeni Malkin and Bryan Rust participated at Pittsburgh Penguins practice Tuesday at the UPMC Lemieux Sports Complex. Malkin appeared to be a full participant, while Rust was in a white, non-contact jersey. Forward Egor Chinakhov did not practice. The team reported he was taking a maintenance day. Malkin missed the team’s two-game road trip last weekend because of an upper-body injury. He has missed four games total this season because of injury and illness. He ranks second on the team with 18 points (six goals, 12 assists). His seemingly minor maladies have afforded the 40-year-old some workload management through the first two months of the season. Rust has not played since Oct. 19. He has been expected to have a lower-body injury re-evaluated early next month. Rust has played in just seven games, recording three goals and two assists. Injured forward Elmer Solderblom skated well prior to practice. We hope to get injury updates after practice. The Penguins, who have lost four straight, host the Calgary Flames on Wednesday in their annual Thanksgiving Eve game. item.title: Retina Dynamics Brings Robotics to the Breaking Boom
item.description: “There are only so many ways breakers can really differentiate themselves in the market. Operational efficiency is one.” Joseph Owens, former Senior Manager of Live Commerce at Fanatics Live, told me that reality was the driving principle behind his new hardware company, Retina Dynamics. Owens founded the company alongside Matthew Harfmann and Sheridan Skala, with founding engineers Jack Scalise and Eli Thummel leading the technical build. During his tenure at Fanatics, Owens identified back-end logistics as one of the single biggest pain point for breakers, noting that almost every major operator struggled with the tedious, time-consuming process of manually sorting cards after massive product releases . To help alleviate the operations backlog, Retina Dynamics is introducing what it claims is the first automated, robotic sorter built explicitly for breakers and sports card consignment sellers . By introducing a robotic sorting machine to the industry, Owens aims to solve that bottleneck without eliminating jobs . The technology is not designed to replace the human workforce; rather, it allows owners to reallocate those employees away from mundane sorting tasks and into roles that drive better business value, such as customer service, expedited shipping, and social marketing . View this post on Instagram A post shared by Joe (@adhdcollector_joe) The Hardware and Safety Measures The solution is a machine roughly the size of a pinball cabinet . The Retina Dynamics robot uses custom-built, in-house scanning software paired with a specialized “claw” to identify, sort, and organize trading cards . Crucially, the machine is designed to safely handle cards whether they are raw, penny-sleeved, or secured in rigid top-loaders . As a secondary benefit, it captures high-resolution, front-and-back scans of every card as it passes through the system, which can be seamlessly exported for consignment listings . According to Owens, extensive testing went into the physics of the claw to ensure the sorting speed matches human efficiency without risking edge or surface damage to the cards . Pricing and Market Availability The systems are currently being assembled in-house by the company’s full-time engineering team . Production is capped at roughly 15 to 20 units per month to ensure quality control and maintain a manageable 120-day lead time for new buyers . Early demand has already outpaced initial supply: Retina Dynamics has sold out of its initial 20-unit run for November and will reopen for additional pre-orders on December 5. The base unit is priced at $25,000, with an additional $450 monthly subscription required to cover the API data costs associated with reading and identifying the cards . For larger operations requiring three or more machines, the hardware price drops to $22,500 per unit . For more information and to view the sorting machines in action, collectors and breakers can visit retinadynamics.ai .

item.title: NBA Champion Spurs analyst takes shot at Luka Doncic, Lakers ahead of clash
item.description: The Lakers’ early-season schedule has been a point of contention, but the team’s biggest test of the season is on Friday when Los Angeles takes on the Spurs. San Antonio earned its 15th win of the season Monday, as did the Lakers. The two West rivals boast the best record in the conference, but Spurs color commentator Sean Elliott isn’t convinced by Los Angeles’ strong start to the campaign. Jacob Tobey and Sean Elliott smiles during the game between the Utah Jazz and San Antonio Spurs at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas on October 9, 2024. NBAE via Getty Images “Well, the Lakers aren’t gonna win the NBA championship. They’re not,” Elliott said bluntly on the game broadcast Monday as San Antonio defeated the Kings. “I mean, they’ll be fun to watch. They have really good players. I like Mamu in a Laker uniform . Plus, your best player always, he’s gotta be a stalwart on the defensive end of the floor. I firmly believe that.” Elliott, a former NBA champion with the Spurs in 1999, built a reputation for being a solid two-way player during his career, particularly on the defensive end of the floor. Clearly, he is not a believer that Doncic has made many strides in that area, despite what many people say. He went on to list the Spurs, Thunder, Knicks and 76ers as potential championship teams . In spite of the mass amount of injuries for Oklahoma City, the former NBA champion believes they have a better chance at this year’s title than the Lakers do. Luka Doncic #77 of the Los Angeles Lakers looks on during the game against the Utah Jazz on November 23, 2026 at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles, California. NBAE via Getty Images San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama walks up court between plays in the second half of an NBA basketball game against the New Orleans Pelicans, Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026, in San Antonio. AP Photo/Darren Abate The heavy usage of Luka Doncic has also been a sticking point for skeptics. Doncic is central to helping the Lakers make a deep playoff run, but many argue his workload is unsustainable throughout the regular season and beyond. Earlier on the broadcast, Elliott praised Doncic for his otherworldly performance this season, but noted that his usage rate quickly puts the purple and gold out of championship contention. He is averaging just over 36 minutes per game. But that is nothing new for the Slovenian sharpshooter. Doncic has averaged between 32 and 37 minutes every season of his nine-year career. Nevertheless, Friday’s game should be a fair litmus test for the Lakers and their skeptics.

item.title: Stacks Opens Bond 4 With 1,050 BTC of Bitcoin Staking Capacity
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Stacks Opens Bond 4 With 1,050 BTC of Bitcoin Staking Capacity GRAND CAYMAN, Cayman Islands, Nov. 24, 2026. Stacks Labs today announced 1,050 BTC of capacity for Bond 4 of Bitcoin staking with Stacks, a Bitcoin layer where BTC holders earn BTC. The bond starts ~Dec. 5, and institutions can register at stacks.co/institutional-bitcoin-staking. Bond 4 carries a 3% target annual yield, paid in BTC weekly over a six-month term. Each BTC staked is paired with STX worth 5% of its value, so filling Bond 4’s 1,050 BTC of capacity requires a corresponding STX commitment. Rewards come from Stacks miners, who commit BTC through Proof of Transfer (PoX), the consensus mechanism Stacks has run since January 2021. Every bond since the Genesis Bond launched in September has filled. 21shares returned for Bond 3, and Bullish (NYSE: BLSH) joined as the first top-10 public Bitcoin treasury company to stake BTC. “Opening more than 1,000 BTC of new capacity for institutions shows how strong the demand for Bitcoin yield has become,” said Muneeb Ali, CEO, Stacks Labs, and founder of Stacks. Institutions can stake from qualified custody, including BitGo. During the bootstrap phase, self-custodial Bitcoin staking is whitelisted. Holders who are not on the whitelist can take part through pooled Bitcoin staking at stacks.co/bitcoin-staking . About Stacks Stacks is a Bitcoin layer where BTC holders earn BTC. With Bitcoin staking, holders stake BTC with STX, and their BTC stays on the Bitcoin L1 under their own custody. Stacks has distributed over 4,200 BTC in rewards to participants since 2021. Learn more at stacks.co . Media contact: Shannon Voight, PR & Events, Stacks Labs, press@stackslabs.com Institutional onboarding: https://www.stacks.co/institutional-bitcoin-staking Disclaimer : This is a sponsored press release. Readers are encouraged to perform their own due diligence before acting on any information presented in this article. item.title: Denny Hamlin Sets Hard Line On NASCAR Retirement Plans
item.description: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Denny Hamlin has made his stance clear to the NASCAR world . The 46-year-old driver plans to end his full-time Cup Series career after the 2027 season. He will not stick around just to fill a seat if his skills fade. This decision comes despite strong pressure from team owner Joe Gibbs to reconsider the timeline. Hamlin told SiriusXM NASCAR Radio that his final call depends entirely on his ability to win races every weekend. Joe Gibbs has been trying to change Hamlin’s mind for some time. The team owner visits the driver’s home in the evenings to discuss the future. Hamlin described these late-night talks on the couch as a normal part of their relationship. “Joe does his normal thing. He just pops in at the house at 8-9 p.m. at night and sits on the couch and has a discussion with you. That’s already started,” Hamlin said, according to MotorBiscuit . The conversations have begun, but the driver’s mind seems set on a specific path. Winning Is the Only Option Hamlin refuses to drive a car he cannot win with. He knows that staying in the sport without a chance at victory would feel wrong. The driver explained that his competitive fire is what keeps him behind the wheel. “If I know that I’m not going to be able to win every single weekend, there’s just no way I can do it,” Hamlin said. This standard is non-negotiable for a driver with his track record. He finished third in the Cup Series standings last year and won four races. The driver also wants to protect the legacy of Joe Gibbs Racing. He plans to ensure the team has a new driver ready before he steps away. Hamlin does not want to leave the organization in a bind or hold back their progress. “I want to make sure they’ve got their next driver planned, lined up — all that stuff. I’m definitely going to do whatever is best for Joe Gibbs Racing, but I’m not going to compromise my performance,” Hamlin said. He values the team but will not sacrifice his own speed to help them. The Clock Is Ticking Hamlin admits that his body feels the toll of racing more than it used to. He senses that his physical edge is slipping away slowly. This feeling in daily life is a warning sign for his time on the track. “I can feel it. In my everyday life, I can tell things are changing. It’s a matter of time before it changes on the racetrack. It just is. I want to avoid that at all costs,” Hamlin said. He wants to leave while he is still at the top of his game. Hamlin is not making this choice based on money or contract terms. He noted that Gibbs has been fair with him throughout his 21-year career. The decision is purely about pride and the desire to compete at the highest level. He feels content with the idea of hanging up his helmet after two more years. Hamlin also said he wants to talk to retired drivers like Kevin Harvick to learn from their experiences.

item.title: Orioles reportedly to sign ex-Mets, Rays ace Freddy Peralta to $125 million deal
item.description: Orioles reportedly to sign ex-Mets, Rays ace Freddy Peralta to $125 million deal originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Heading into the 2026 MLB offseason, the Baltimore Orioles needed to make one huge addition: a front-line starting pitcher. Trevor Rogers hit the open market and reportedly signed with the Chicago Cubs . But the Orioles weren't looking in Rogers' direction. They had been eyeing up a different starting pitcher and were gearing up to make a splash before Thanksgiving. According to Ken Rosenthal of The Athletic , that's exactly what the Orioles did, as they've reportedly signed Freddy Peralta to a huge five-year, $125 million contract. Orioles to sign Freddy Peralta after wild 2026 season "Free-agent right-hander Freddy Peralta in agreement with Orioles on five-year, $125M contract, pending physical, sources tell @TheAthletic," Rosenthal reports. "No deferrals, no opt-outs in deal." This is a big addition for the Orioles, as they had just lost Rogers to the Cubs the night before this deal was reported by Rosenthal. The new-look Orioles rotation will be headlined by Peralta, alongside Kyle Bradish, Shane Baz, Brandon Young, Cade Povich, and Trey Gibson, among others. Peralta, the 30-year-old right-hander, is a two-time All-Star and just won ALCS MVP with the Tampa Bay Rays after being picked up at the 2026 MLB trade deadline. MORE : Full contract details on Tarik Skubal’s reported $450M deal with Mets He had a horrible start to the 2026 season, posting a 4.99 ERA in22 starts with the Mets before he was dealt to the Rays, and rediscovered what made him elite. In 10 starts for the Rays in the regular season, he posted a 3.25 ERA with 1.2 bWAR, easily surpassing the -0.5 bWAR he had in his time with the Mets. Come the postseason, Peralta's 2.95 ERA in five appearances, four starts, and across 21.1 innings with 16 strikeouts helped the Rays make the World Series. This is a huge addition for the Orioles, as Peralta is now set to stick in Baltimore for the next five seasons at $25 million per-year. It's expensive, but the Orioles now have added one of the best starting pitchers available this offseason, not named Tarik Skubal. item.title: Homo erectus lived in the rainforest alongside Denisovans
item.description: Homo erectus was walking around mainland Asia at least 60,000 years more recently than archaeologists thought. A handful of teeth from two caves in southern China's Guangxi Province just filled in a significant gap in the fossil record of a region that's vital to the story of how our genus, Homo , took over the world. The chemical makeup of the teeth's enamel suggests that, over the course of their lives, these Homo erectus moved across surprisingly large distances and made their living in dense tropical rainforests—an environment we'd previously assumed that only our species had ever gained a real foothold in. And one of the teeth offers a strong clue that Homo erectus probably shared this vast landscape with the Denisovans. A handful of teeth with a lot to say Baxian and Naxian are a pair of limestone caves that lie 15 kilometers apart along a karst valley corridor in southern China. University of Copenhagen paleoanthropologist Frido Welker and his colleagues unearthed a total of nine hominin teeth from among the more than 18,000 bones and fragments from non-hominin animals found there. Macquarie University paleoanthropologist Kira Westaway and her colleagues analyzed proteins and chemical isotopes from the enamel of five of these teeth. Read full article Comments

item.title: Why Packers’ Offensive Line Could Look Different After Bye
item.description: Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur. Getty (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) Getty The Green Bay Packers offensive line has had anything but continuity through the 2026 season. While head coach Matt LaFleur admitted that this has been a major issue for the team, he also acknowledged that there is a chance for them to find continuity between their bye week and the end of the season. “I think continuity is critical,” said LaFleur when discussing offensive line continuity. “Especially when you’re talking about the offensive line, where you need five guys working as one. So I think that is a huge component in terms of your ability to go out there and have consistent success.” The Packers coach added that experience is also important. “I also think just, you know, the experience of that group up front plays a pivotal role in that as well,” added LaFleur. The Packers have only had Jordan Morgan at left tackle start every game at the same position. They have had multiple starters at the four other spots. Green Bay Packers Hoping to Find Offensive Line Continuity Getty (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) Now, the team has a chance to find some continuity. Jordan Morgan is still at left tackle and Anthony Belton has been starting at right tackle since Week 3. They are high on Laken Tomlinson at left guard, and if Kevin Zeitler and Sean Rhyan are healthy, they are going to start at right guard and center, respectively. As long as there are not any injuries this unit is going to be what leads the team into a playoff push. While LaFleur is excited to see the continuity, his message to the unit is to handle what they have to. “You know, my thing is this: it really— at the end of the day, it doesn’t matter,” said LaFleur. “You got a job to go, and you got to go perform well. And if you don’t, then it’s going to get scrutinized, and it is what it is. But it’s never an excuse. You still— that’s why you prepare everybody.” Packers Not Making Excuses LaFleur noted that he thinks that everyone on the roster needs to be ready to be called into duty. “I mean, whether you’re on the active or you’re a P-squad guy, you got to be ready to play, and you got to be ready to do your part. So it’s just— it’s the circumstance that every team in the league faces.” It almost comes off as if LaFleur realized in his first answer that he was making an excuse of not having continuity and then tried to defend it by saying that the depth has to be ready. Still, depth or not, those players would be best with continuity and experience as well We will see how many games Green Bay can roll with their projected five. They play the Los Angeles Rams in Week 12. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Why Packers’ Offensive Line Could Look Different After Bye appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Preview: Eintracht travel to Stuttgart
item.description: Preview: Eintracht travel to Stuttgart Boosted by their victory over Hoffenheim, the Eagles take on direct rivals VfB Stuttgart away from home on Saturday evening – a fixture which is almost guaranteed to produce goals. Looking to build consistency Following Saturday’s 1-0 home win over TSG Hoffenheim, Adi Hütter’s Eintracht Frankfurt side have picked up seven points from their last three Bundesliga assignments, lifting them into seventh place in the standings. “We have a young team that wants to become even more consistent, and these are exactly the types of games that help us build confidence and gain experience,” said Eagles sporting director Timmo Hardung. “We want to build on that in Stuttgart.” Opponents VfB, who drew 0-0 at promoted FC Schalke 04 last time out, are currently two points behind Eintracht in eighth spot. “We know it won’t be an easy game but if we build on our recent performances, battle together and stay compact, we have a good chance of picking up another three points,” said Oscar Højlund. Steeped in tradition Saturday evening’s primetime fixture (kick-off 18:30 CET) is one with a lot of history. The two teams are facing each other for the 107th time in the Bundesliga on Matchday 11, with Stuttgart boasting 45 wins to Eintracht’s 37. The sides have shared the spoils on 24 occasions, including in their most recent meeting on Matchday 34 last term, when they played out a 2-2 draw. Goals guaranteed There has not been a goalless draw between the Eagles and VfB since 26 May 1994, when goalkeepers Uli Stein and Eike Immel both kept clean sheets in the City Forest. Remarkably, 61 years have passed since the last stalemate between the sides in Stuttgart. Peter Kunter was in goal for Eintracht that day, with the likes of Friedel Lutz, Dieter Lindner and Jürgen Grabowski also featuring in the game on 18 September 1965. This weekend, Hütter’s charges will be perfectly happy with a repeat of the narrow win they secured against Hoffenheim last time out. “That gives us momentum and confidence,” said Elias Baum. “We’re in great spirits. In the next few games, we’ll try to keep it going. Hopefully, at the end of the year, we’ll be in a position that enables us to keep looking up the table.” The Eagles have four more league games before Christmas, as well as a DFB-Pokal last-16 tie against Borussia Dortmund. For now, though, their focus is firmly on Stuttgart this Saturday.
