item.title: Atiku has youth support despite Tinubu’s control of Lagos, says Momodu
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye African Democratic Congress (ADC) chieftain Dele Momodu has defended former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar’s appeal to young voters, saying Atiku has never controlled a state while President Bola Tinubu exercises strong political influence in Lagos. Momodu spoke in an interview on Arise Television on Tuesday, discussing Atiku’s chances in the 2027 election, age dynamics, political influence and efforts by opposition parties to agree on a consensus candidate. “If he’s not connecting to the youths, you won’t see people shouting ‘Bamayi’ all over Nigeria. I just watched your programme now in Kogi State. The people on the streets are not geriatrics; they are young people,” he said. The ADC chieftain argued that age should not be used to judge a candidate’s ability to connect with voters. Citing his own presidential bid, he said: “I contested 15 years ago, at the age of 51 to be president of Nigeria. Why didn’t I win? It’s not about age.” He said Atiku was surrounded by young supporters and described him as “a completely detribalised Nigerian” and “an employer of labour.” Comparing Atiku’s political influence with Tinubu’s, Momodu said, “He has never held on to any state. Tinubu controls Lagos, life and death. Tinubu controls Lagos and Atiku does not control anywhere.” On talks to select a consensus opposition candidate, Momodu pointed to Atiku’s past willingness to step aside for another candidate. “In 1993, I was 33 years old when Alhaji Atiku Abubakar first came out to run as a potential candidate of SDP, and at that time, he stepped down for MKO Abiola without making any trouble. After that, he was expected to be the running mate, he didn’t get it. He never fought anybody. He then contested in his state and became governor before they now made him running mate to President Olusegun Obasanjo. He has pursued his dreams with uncommon equanimity,” he said. The post Atiku has youth support despite Tinubu’s control of Lagos, says Momodu appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Microsoft brings serverless PostgreSQL into Fabric to bridge transactions and analytics
item.description: Microsoft has brought its HorizonDB PostgreSQL service into public preview in Fabric, aiming to bring transactional and analytical workloads closer together. The corporation says applications can submit queries through a single PostgreSQL endpoint, with transactional and analytical work handled by the appropriate engines. Analysts said the move follows similar efforts by Databricks and Snowflake to combine operational databases with analytics. But tighter integration with Microsoft's stack could make applications harder to move elsewhere. Fabric HorizonDB joins SQL database and Cosmos DB in Microsoft's Fabric database portfolio. "By bringing operational databases, analytics, and AI together on a unified, governed platform, developers can build intelligent applications with less data movement and complexity. Fabric HorizonDB will also serve as the PostgreSQL backend for Fabric apps," Microsoft said. Microsoft first unveiled Azure HorizonDB in preview in November 2025 and made it generally available last week. It competes with other cloud database services and distributed systems such as CockroachDB and YugabyteDB, both of which support PostgreSQL's wire protocol. At the time, it said HorizonDB would offer "massive read scale without the need to replicate the database between instances." Speaking to The Register last week, Shireesh Thota, veep of Azure databases and Fabric applications, said that bringing the system into Fabric – its platform for data lakes, data warehouses, and analytics launched in 2023 – would connect operational data in HorizonDB with analytical data in OneLake, Fabric's unified data lake. "Once the data hits the OneLake storage, you can have analytical engines that take advantage of it. In HorizonDB, the PostgreSQL query engine can talk to the distributed query engine that we use in our Fabric data warehouse. We're fusing these query engines, thereby enabling the developers to submit a query that has pieces of the query that can work on OLTP and pieces of the query that can work on OLAP," he said. "The application need not worry about two endpoints, or about consistency of data and all that complexity. They can just talk to HorizonDB as a Fabric endpoint, and they can submit all these queries. We are basically operationalizing in OneLake." Operational data remains in HorizonDB's database storage, while mirroring maintains an analytical copy in OneLake, introduced in 2023 , which replicates a snapshot of the external database to OneLake in Delta Parquet tables and keeps the replica synced in "near real time." Thota said the process would not affect the transactional system. "Our core goal is to never impact OLTP workload while we are doing this, and we succeed [by] reading off the log as an additional replica to do this mirroring," he said. But the overall plan of putting serverless PostgreSQL OLTP in an analytics platform, bringing it close to OLAP systems, is one some vendors are already executing to meet the demands of new A

item.description: The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has announced its decision to boycott a security meeting convened by the Inspector-General of Police, citing alleged attacks on its members and what it described as the police’s failure to protect opposition figures. The party said it no longer felt safe under the Nigeria Police Force, accusing security agencies of failing to prevent repeated attacks on its members allegedly carried out by thugs loyal to the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC). The NDC announced its position in a statement signed by its National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, on Monday. It said it would not legitimise a security process that had failed to protect its members, adding that the alleged violence had become an intolerable pattern across the country. The party cited incidents in Benue, Edo, Calabar, Enugu and Delta states, including an alleged attempt by APC loyalists to prevent its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, from entering Benue State. It accused the APC-led government of turning political campaigns into battlefields, where the safety of opposition members could no longer be guaranteed. The NDC also alleged that security personnel were complicit in the violence, particularly the alleged attack on the campaign team of its Delta Central senatorial candidate, Ovie Omo-Agege, in Delta State. Omo-Agege is a chieftain of the NDC. Gunmen reportedly attacked Omo-Agege’s campaign convoy in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area. The former deputy senate president escaped unhurt, according to his media adviser, Sunny Areh. The attack initially left four campaign members dead, according to the Omo-Agege Campaign Organisation. However, the Nigeria Police Force said preliminary reports indicated that six people were killed, while several others sustained injuries. Police Speak The police, in a statement issued on Tuesday by its Force Public Relations Officer, said an investigation had been launched to establish the circumstances surrounding the attack and determine the verified casualty figure. Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, directed the Delta State Commissioner of Police to conduct a thorough, impartial and evidence-based investigation. The police said the investigation would examine the sequence of events, identify those responsible and establish the circumstances surrounding the shooting, including the deployment and conduct of officers at the scene. It added that any officer found to have acted negligently or breached professional standards would face disciplinary action, while anyone found culpable of criminal offences would be prosecuted. The NDC, however, accused the police of displaying bias and failing to investigate previous attacks on its members or bring those responsible to justice. item.title: CAS explains decision to restore Senegal’s AFCON title
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) has explained why it overturned the Confederation of African Football’s (CAF) decision to award Morocco the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations title, ruling that Senegal’s 1-0 victory in the final must stand. In a media release on Tuesday, the court said both teams had returned to the pitch and expressed their willingness to continue before the referee, Jean-Jacques Ndala, blew his whistle to resume play in the 109th minute. It explained that the referee’s decision to restart or stop the match fell within his authority, adding that the effects of his decision were limited to the pitch and therefore covered by the ‘field of play’ doctrine. “After having examined the arguments raised by the Parties, the Arbitral Panel considered that the Referee’s decision to resume the match or to stop it fell definitively within his sole authority. By blowing his whistle to restart play, the Referee considered that the conditions for resuming the match had been met – both teams were on the pitch again, and both expressed their willingness to resume,” the statement said. CAS also ruled that Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON regulations, relied upon by Morocco in its challenge, did not apply to the circumstances of the final. According to the court, the provisions are intended to determine the outcome of a match when a team’s conduct leads the referee to abandon the game permanently. The court further rejected the description of the referee’s decision as ‘arbitrary’, acknowledging the extreme tension surrounding the match but stating that his judgment did not appear to have been influenced by external factors. Consequently, CAS upheld the appeal filed by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF), set aside the CAF Appeal Board’s decision and reinstated the decision of CAF’s Disciplinary Board. The ruling confirms Senegal’s 1-0 victory over Morocco in the January 18 final, restoring the West African nation as AFCON 2025 champions. CAF had previously declared Senegal to have forfeited the final after the team temporarily left the pitch in protest during the match, awarding Morocco a 3-0 victory. The decision was unanimous among the three-member CAS panel. The post CAS explains decision to restore Senegal’s AFCON title appeared first on Vanguard News .

The union also directed chapters that have yet to join the ongoing industrial action to commence the strike immediately, warning that failure to address its demands could result in an indefinite shutdown of academic activities in the affected institutions. ASUP Zone D, which covers the South-East and South-South geopolitical zones, announced the directive at a press briefing in Enugu on Tuesday by its Zonal Coordinator, Comrade Dr Iloma U. Richard. The union said the strike followed the failure of the affected state governments to implement the Consolidated Academic Tools Allowance (CATA), Earned Academic Allowance (EAA) and other components of the ASUP/FGN 2026 renegotiated agreement. It recalled that the Federal Government and ASUP signed the agreement on April 8, 2026, with implementation of the allowances taking effect from January 2026. According to the union, while the Federal Government has commenced implementation of the agreement for lecturers in federal polytechnics, several state governments have failed to extend the benefits to academic staff in their institutions. It said its national leadership had written to state governors on August 10 and September 21, 2026, appealing for the implementation of the allowances but received disappointing responses from some states. The union said the National Executive Council, at its 118th regular meeting held on October 22 in Abuja, subsequently issued a 15-day ultimatum to the affected state governments, beginning October 27, to address the matter. “Having exhaustively explored measures to persuade concerned states to comply, the national leadership was constrained to direct all chapters in the states that were yet to comply to proceed on strike with effect from November 12, 2026,” the union said. ASUP, however, noted that some states had responded positively, listing Yobe, Kano, Ondo, Bayelsa, Niger, Abia, Taraba, Plateau, Nasarawa, Zamfara, Jigawa and Rivers as states that had approved the implementation of CATA and EAA. It added that engagements with Delta, Akwa Ibom and Katsina states were also progressing positively. Enugu lecturers’ welfare Beyond the allowances, the union expressed particular concern over what it described as years of neglect of academic staff welfare in Enugu State-owned institutions, particularly the Institute of Management and Technology (IMT), Enugu, and Enugu State Polytechnic, Iwollo. It alleged that lecturers in the two institutions were yet to benefit from the prevailing minimum wage, wage awards and the 35 per cent and 25 per cent salary reviews approved in 2023. item.title: Full List: 10 countries with most AFCON titles
item.description: Egypt remain the most successful country in the history of the Africa Cup of Nations, AFCON with seven titles, followed by Cameroon and Ghana, who have won the continental competition five and four times respectively. Nigeria are among five countries in the top four positions, having lifted the trophy three times since making their debut at the tournament. The Super Eagles won their first AFCON title in 1980, when Nigeria hosted the competition and defeated Algeria 3-0 in the final. They secured their second crown in Tunisia in 1994, beating Zambia 2-1, before claiming their third title in South Africa in 2013 with a 1-0 victory over Burkina Faso. Côte d’Ivoire are also three-time champions, having won the tournament in 1992, 2015 and 2023. Egypt lead the all-time standings with seven titles, having dominated the competition in its early years and later enjoyed a remarkable run of three consecutive championships in 2006, 2008 and 2010. Cameroon occupy second place with five titles, while Ghana are third with four. Ghana’s last triumph came in 1982, while Cameroon’s most recent success was in 2017. Algeria and the Democratic Republic of the Congo have each won the competition twice. Algeria claimed their titles in 1990 and 2019, while DR Congo won in 1968 and 1974, when the country competed under the names Congo-Kinshasa and Zaire. Morocco are also credited with two titles, following the Confederation of African Football’s March 2026 decision to award them the 2025 AFCON trophy. Senegal had initially won the final 1-0 after extra time, but CAF’s Appeal Board later ruled that the Senegalese team had forfeited the match and recorded a 3-0 victory for Morocco. Senegal subsequently appealed the decision to the Court of Arbitration for Sport, which was expected to issue its ruling on November 24, 2026. The outcome of that appeal could affect the official title record. Seven other countries have won the AFCON title once. They are Ethiopia, Sudan, Congo, South Africa, Tunisia, Zambia and Senegal. Below is the ranking of countries by the number of AFCON titles won: Egypt – 7 titles: 1957, 1959, 1986, 1998, 2006, 2008 and 2010. Cameroon – 5 titles: 1984, 1988, 2000, 2002 and 2017. Ghana – 4 titles: 1963, 1965, 1978 and 1982. Nigeria – 3 titles: 1980, 1994 and 2013. Côte d’Ivoire – 3 titles: 1992, 2015 and 2023. Algeria – 2 titles: 1990 and 2019. DR Congo – 2 titles: 1968 and 1974 Senegal – 2 titles: 2021, 2025 Ethiopia – 1 title: 1962. Sudan – 1 title: 1970. Congo – 1 title: 1972. South Africa – 1 title: 1996. Tunisia – 1 title: 2004. Zambia – 1 title: 2012. Morocco – 1 title: 1976 Vanguard News The post Full List: 10 countries with most AFCON titles appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: US blacklists Megaspeed hours after Jensen Huang returns to Nvidia
item.description: Jensen Huang was barely back in charge of Nvidia when Uncle Sam slapped Megaspeed –­ the Singaporean cloud provider at the center of the scandal that cost him his job ­­– on its trade blacklist. The US Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) has added Megaspeed and a number of affiliated businesses to its Entity List, restricting their access to American technology amid an ongoing investigation into the suspected diversion of advanced GPUs to China. The final rule [PDF], filed Monday afternoon and scheduled for publication in the Federal Register on Wednesday, names seven businesses across Singapore, Malaysia, and Thailand, including Megaspeed's owner, Swiftdata, and Malaysian subsidiary Speedmatrix. Also in Washington's crosshairs is Apex Enterprise Solutions, a Singapore-based subsidiary of Chinese cloud computing giant Alibaba. BIS said the businesses posed a significant risk of diverting advanced computing hardware to recipients or applications not authorized by the US government. Anyone looking to supply the seven companies with goods subject to US export controls will need a license, with applications subject to a "presumption of denial." Despite the timing of Monday's announcement, the US government's interest in Megaspeed predates the revelations about Jensen Huang's private life by some considerable margin. In a joint statement issued last week, the Departments of Justice and Commerce confirmed that the latter had opened an investigation into Megaspeed in 2024 after spotting suspicious activity while monitoring potential violations of semiconductor export controls. Investigators requested records from Nvidia relating to both direct and indirect sales to Megaspeed in May 2025, and the GPU giant put the Singaporean outfit on its internal "no sell" list the following month. US investigators, accompanied by Singaporean law enforcement officials, subsequently visited Megaspeed's premises and interviewed its then-CEO, Alice Huang. The Justice Department has since taken the lead on the criminal investigation. Alice Huang, who is not related to the Nvidia boss, is a businesswoman with whom Jensen was said to be having an affair – he admitted to extramarital infidelity earlier this month , although he never name-checked the Megaspeed exec. According to reports, US intelligence officials suspected she was working on behalf of Chinese intelligence, though Beijing has rejected the espionage allegations. Megaspeed maintains that its business is lawful and says Alice Huang formally left the company in August last year. It has also enlisted outside lawyers to conduct an internal investigation. Nvidia's own Huang lasted all of 11 days in corporate exile. The chipmaker's board unanimously voted to reinstate its co-founder as president and CEO on Monday, less than a week after board chairman Harvey Jones indicated that bringing him back wasn't on the cards. item.title: I’ll continue to criticise Atiku for attacking Tinubu – Shettima
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Vice-President Kashim Shettima has defended his right to criticise African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, saying he would not hold back in defending President Bola Tinubu against political attacks. Shettima, who described Atiku as an elder statesman whom he holds in high regard, said their political differences would not prevent him from expressing his views about the former vice-president. He spoke on Tuesday in Maiduguri, Borno State’s capital, during the inauguration of the North-East Development Commission’s multi-sectoral development interventions. “We respect former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar. He is an elder statesman we hold in very high esteem, but as a Fulani man, I have the right to throw stones at him. And he has to endure strictly whatever stones I throw at him,” he said. The vice president also cautioned against attempts to portray political disagreements as personal hostility, saying he was willing to maintain cordial relationships with opposition figures as long as they did not attack his principal. “So long as they do not attack my boss, we will practise politics of maturity, politics without bitterness, and politics of tolerance because what binds us together surpasses whatever that divides us,” he said. Shettima also identified former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi and former Kano State Governor Rabiu Kwankwaso as his friends, while describing Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde as a personal friend. He said he had never insulted Makinde, adding that political differences should not undermine relationships among leaders. The vice-president urged Nigerians to make informed decisions ahead of the 2027 presidential election, arguing that the Tinubu administration’s economic policies were beginning to yield results. Shettima also ruled out a return to petrol subsidy, saying its removal and the realignment of multiple exchange rates were necessary to prevent the economy from collapsing. “The president has a great deal of human empathy for the Nigerian people. He withdrew the subsidy, not to inflict pain on Nigerians. No, he removed the subsidy to save the Nigerian economy from collapse,” he said. He further accused some Nigerians who had benefited from the previous economic arrangements of sponsoring anti-government sentiments. Calling for restraint among political actors, Shettima urged candidates to accept the outcome of the 2027 election rather than resort to threats and actions capable of creating tension. He expressed confidence that Nigerians would vote massively for Tinubu on January 16, adding that there were no polling booths on Facebook, Instagram or other social media platforms. The post I’ll continue to criticise Atiku for attacking Tinubu – Shettima appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Senate orders scrutiny of revised 2025 laws
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Senate has called for a thorough scrutiny of the revised and consolidated Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2025, to ensure accuracy before granting legislative approval. The President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio, made the call on Tuesday while reading a letter from President Bola Tinubu seeking the National Assembly’s approval of the revised compendium. Akpabio said the Senate must ensure that all amendments were accurately reflected and that no provisions had been altered from the original laws passed by the National Assembly. He said it was necessary to compare the compiled laws with the versions passed by both chambers to prevent discrepancies that could undermine the country’s legal framework. In the letter, Tinubu said the committee constituted on October 24, 2024, examined 932 federal enactments and 731 subsidiary legislations. He disclosed that 664 principal enactments were validated for inclusion in the revised compendium, while 268 were identified as obsolete, spent or repealed. According to the President, the updated compendium would provide a reliable legal reference for the judiciary, legal practitioners, government institutions, investors and the general public. The Senate subsequently referred the revised compendium to the Committees on Rules and Business and Judiciary for further legislative action. Contributing to the debate, former Senate Leader, Senator Yahaya Abdullahi (APC, Kebbi North), described the exercise as important to Nigeria’s legal system and the administration of justice. He recalled that a similar exercise was conducted after the return to democratic governance in 1999 to give legitimacy to decrees enacted under military administrations. Abdullahi, who noted that the last official consolidation of the laws was undertaken in 2004, said the current exercise had become necessary after more than two decades. He, however, cautioned against rushing the process, given its implications for the country’s legal system and justice delivery. He proposed that the compendium be thoroughly examined by the Senate Committee on Judiciary, Human Rights and Legal Matters, with the support of competent legal experts. According to him, the committee should analyse the volumes and present a comprehensive report to enable lawmakers to understand the proposed changes before approval. Also contributing, Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Jibrin Barau (APC, Kano North), supported the call for scrutiny, warning that even a single altered clause could make the compilation inconsistent with the laws passed by the National Assembly. Barau recommended that the consolidated provisions be compared with the original versions passed by both chambers and those assented to by the President. Akpabio agreed with the submissions, saying the Senate usually engaged consultants and relevant experts to examine such documents before presenting a summarised report. item.title: UniCredit Opens Bitcoin to Italian Savers, Capping Gains at 65%
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine UniCredit Opens Bitcoin to Italian Savers, Capping Gains at 65% UniCredit on Tuesday began selling a capital-protected certificate that lets retail clients in Italy follow the bitcoin price, a product the bank calls the first investment solution of its kind in the country. The six-year, euro-denominated certificate will be listed on the Munich stock exchange and is linked to the iShares Bitcoin ETP managed by BlackRock, UniCredit said in a release. The placement period runs from Nov. 24 to Dec. 18, 2026. The note is open only to UniCredit Italia retail clients with specific characteristics, and only through the bank’s advisory service. It can’t be bought independently or by investors who aren’t UniCredit clients, and the minimum investment is €1,000, Italian newswire Teleborsa reported . How the certificate works A capital-protected certificate is a structured note. The issuing bank promises to repay the original investment at maturity and pays a return tied to an underlying asset, in this case bitcoin through the BlackRock product. Buyers hold a claim on the bank, not bitcoin itself. If bitcoin is down at maturity, holders get 100% of their capital back. If it rises, they share in the gain up to a maximum return of 65% on the capital invested. Before maturity, the certificate’s price follows market conditions, so the protection applies only at the end of the six years. That cap works out to roughly 8.7% a year at most, no matter how far bitcoin climbs. And because the certificate is UniCredit’s own debt, the protection depends on the bank’s ability to pay. Documents for a similar UniCredit note in Germany state that no third-party guarantee covers an issuer default. “With the launch of this certificate, UniCredit is writing a new page of financial innovation in the country, confirming its market leadership,” said Chicco Di Stasi, Head of Group Investment Product Solutions at UniCredit. “Diversification is no longer just a prudential rule, but the key to capturing the value of the future,” Di Stasi said, adding that the bank is responding to growing client demand and offering the product to Italian savers “for the very first time.” Built on notes sold in Germany and Austria Di Stasi said the bank is bringing to Italy “a pioneering model already proven by its success in Germany and Austria.” Those earlier notes are denominated in dollars and track BlackRock’s U.S.-listed iShares Bitcoin Trust instead. HypoVereinsbank, UniCredit’s German unit, sold a version to private clients in March with a 160% cap, or 60% upside. UniCredit Bank Austria launched its own six-year note in April with a 175% cap, or 75% upside. Italy’s 65% falls between the two. The bank has moved into bitcoin in steps. It first offered a capital-protected bitcoin product to professional clients only in 2025. In May, it placed a bitcoin and ether certificate for professional clients with a €100,000 minimum. item.title: How Trump and Silicon Valley forced Nvidia to take Jensen Huang back
item.description: On Monday morning, Jensen Huang walked into Nvidia’s Santa Clara headquarters to rapturous applause from employees lining the walkways above him. Huang was visibly moved as one colleague threw themselves into his arms for a hug. The spectacular reinstatement of the chief executive of Nvidia, less than two weeks after he resigned in a scandal over an affair with a customer and suspected Chinese spy—as well as a second reported affair with a subordinate—caught even the company’s most senior executives by surprise. The abrupt reversal by Nvidia’s board was spurred by President Donald Trump, who applied pressure to the board over the weekend after watching what was once America’s most valuable company as well as the wider tech sector haemorrhage value last week. item.title: Reps advance bills to reform social investment agency, regulate eye care
item.description: By Gift Chapi Odekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has passed two bills seeking to reform Nigeria’s social investment programmes and strengthen the regulation of optometry and dispensing opticians through second reading. The bills, sponsored by Deputy Speaker Benjamin Kalu and other lawmakers, are aimed at improving the delivery of social protection programmes and addressing regulatory gaps in the country’s eye care sector. Leading the debate on the proposed amendment to the National Social Investment Programme Agency (Establishment) Act, 2023, Kalu said the success of social investment programmes should be measured not by the size of their budgets or the number of initiatives introduced, but by their actual impact on vulnerable Nigerians. He described social investment as a commitment by the Nigerian state to prevent temporary hardship from becoming permanent exclusion. The Deputy Speaker said the growing scale and complexity of Nigeria’s social protection system had made it necessary to strengthen the institutional framework for coordinating, implementing and monitoring interventions. According to him, the proposed amendment would address administrative fragmentation, duplication of beneficiaries, unreliable data and inadequate coordination among the different levels of government. Among its major provisions is the introduction of the Grant for Vulnerable Groups Programme and the National Social Safety-Net Coordinating Office as components of the agency. The bill also seeks to establish the National Social Safety-Net Coordinating Office as the central institution for coordinating and managing data on national social safety nets, including maintaining, updating and verifying the National Social Register. Kalu said the proposed legislation would also provide for the establishment of state offices to bring programme implementation closer to beneficiaries and introduce executive directors with clearly defined responsibilities for individual programmes. He explained that the changes would strengthen accountability, improve coordination and ensure that government assistance reached intended beneficiaries. He identified children requiring support to remain in school, unemployed youths seeking economic opportunities and vulnerable households needing temporary assistance as some of those expected to benefit from a more coordinated social investment system. The 15-clause bill was subsequently subjected to a voice vote by the Speaker, Abbas Tajudeen, and received the support of lawmakers. In a related development, the House also passed second reading a bill seeking to repeal the Optometrists and Dispensing Opticians (Registration, etc.) Act, Cap. 09, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2004, and introduce a new regulatory framework for the profession. The proposed legislation, sponsored by Kalu and eight other lawmakers, seeks to establish the Optometrists and Dispensing Opticians Registration Council of Nigeria to regulate professional training and

item.title: Senegal Regain AFCON Title After Appeal
item.description: Senegal on Tuesday regained their Africa Cup of Nations title after winning an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) against the decision by the Confederation of African Football to declare Morocco the winners following a chaotic final in January. “The Court of Arbitration for Sport has upheld the appeal by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) against the Confederation of African Football (CAF) and the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF) concerning the final of the Africa Cup of Nations Morocco 2025,” CAS said in a statement. The Swiss-based sports court said Senegal’s appeal had been upheld by “a unanimous decision”, and their original 1-0 victory after extra time is reinstated. In March, the Confederation of African Football (CAF) sensationally overturned the result of the final, awarding Morocco a 3-0 victory, and the title, after many Senegalese players walked off the pitch in protest at a penalty given to the hosts with the game still goalless. Senegal and Morocco players line up prior the Africa Cup of Nations (CAN) final football match between Senegal and Morocco at the Prince Moulay Abdellah Stadium in Rabat on January 18, 2026. Photo by PAUL ELLIS / AFP The CAF Appeals Committee had justified its decision to overturn the result and declare Morocco champions based on Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON Regulations. Those state that if a team “refuses to play or leaves the ground before the regular end of the match without the authorisation of the referee, it shall be considered (loser) and shall be eliminated for good from the current competition”. However, the Senegal players eventually returned to the pitch and the final carried on. The CAS panel therefore considered that the referee’s decision to restart the final showed that “the conditions for resuming the match had been met”, and that articles 82 and 84 were therefore “not applicable in this case”. item.title: 2027 polls: NUC considers four-week university break
item.description: …Mobilises VCs to support INEC as commission plans 57,000 additional BVAS machines By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The National Universities Commission (NUC) is considering a three-to-four-week adjustment of academic calendars across Nigerian universities to enable academics to participate in the conduct of the 2027 general elections. The proposed adjustment is part of efforts by the commission to mobilise Vice-Chancellors and university authorities nationwide to provide credible and non-partisan academic personnel, particularly as Collation and Returning Officers. The NUC Executive Secretary, Prof. Abdullahi Yusufu Ribadu, disclosed this on Monday in Abuja when the Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan, SAN, led a delegation of National Commissioners and senior officials on a courtesy visit to the commission. Ribadu said the NUC would engage Vice-Chancellors on the nomination of qualified academics for electoral assignments, adding that an online meeting would be convened to facilitate the process. He also pledged to issue a formal circular to universities upon receiving an official request from INEC, stressing that the credibility of the 2027 elections would depend significantly on the integrity of personnel deployed to conduct them. “Since we want to have credible elections, we also have to have credible personnel,” he said. The NUC boss explained that the proposed adjustment of academic calendars would give academics sufficient time to discharge their electoral responsibilities without compromising students’ academic programmes. According to him, the proposed break would not exceed four weeks, adding that the commission would consult university administrators to ensure that the arrangement neither disrupted academic activities nor interfered with INEC’s electoral timetable. “We will discuss with the Vice-Chancellors and have their calendars tweaked in such a way that it will not affect the elections, nor will it affect the studies of the students,” he said. Ribadu also stressed that academics and other ad hoc officials engaged in the electoral process must demonstrate absolute neutrality, proposing that they take an oath of neutrality before deployment. Beyond providing election officials, the NUC Executive Secretary proposed a broader institutional partnership between universities and INEC, including student internship opportunities at the electoral commission, joint research initiatives and possible academic programmes in electoral studies. He identified artificial intelligence, robotics and data analytics as areas where Nigerian universities could collaborate with INEC to strengthen electoral administration and improve the country’s democratic process. The NUC also proposed leveraging student organisations, campus clubs and other university platforms to intensify voter education and combat misinformation and disinformation ahead of the elections. item.title: Delta killings: Turaki-led PDP urges presidency to renounce ‘war rhetoric’ ahead of 2027
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — The Kabiru Tanimu Turaki-led Interim National Working Committee (INWC) of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has blamed President Bola Tinubu’s past political statements for what it described as a growing climate of violence against opposition parties, following the killing of at least four persons in an attack on a Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) campaign in Delta State. The group said the attack in Uduere, Ughelli North, where gunmen opened fire while former Deputy Senate President and NDC Delta Central senatorial candidate, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, was addressing supporters, exposed the dangers of inflammatory political rhetoric ahead of the 2027 general elections. In a statement by its National Publicity Secretary, Comrade Ini Ememobong, on Tuesday, the INWC demanded that Tinubu publicly renounce his previous remarks, which it accused of encouraging hostility towards opposition parties. The statement cited Tinubu’s 2022 declaration that political power must be “grabbed, snatched and run away with”, as well as his 2026 remark that “all is fair in politics”, as examples of what it described as dangerous political messaging. “These two statements alone, coming from their leader, were the adrenaline that APC followers needed to unleash unmitigated mayhem on opposition parties,” it alleged. It also cited alleged threats by some APC figures, including Senator Fadahunsi of Osun State, the Chairman of Kuje Area Council and the party’s Edo State chairman, against citizens unwilling to vote for the ruling party. On Delta State, the group alleged that intimidation of opposition figures had become recurrent, claiming that at least two deadly attacks against opposition groups had occurred in November alone. It further alleged that the incidents were widely believed to have been sponsored by the APC. “With this latest attack and the deaths and injuries it caused, the world can now clearly see the fruits of the evil seed planted by the APC through violent communication,” the statement said. The INWC also demanded a thorough and transparent investigation into the attack, urging the police to make their findings public. It called on the Inspector-General of Police to ensure that the investigation he ordered was conducted professionally and that other political attacks across the country received similar attention. It urged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), the National Peace Committee and election observers to identify and publicly expose individuals responsible for political violence, including through international platforms. The group also raised concerns over allegations that police personnel were present at the scene but failed to assist victims, calling on security agencies, particularly the police, to demonstrate neutrality and professionalism. “Nigerians need responsible leadership that does not sacrifice the peace and unity of the country at the altar of political domination and elections,” it said.

item.title: South Korea Unveils Crypto Bill Capping Exchange Ownership at 20%
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine South Korea Unveils Crypto Bill Capping Exchange Ownership at 20% South Korea’s Financial Services Commission on Tuesday unveiled a government bill that would cap a major shareholder’s stake in a crypto exchange at 20%, open the door to domestic coin offerings and let bank-led groups issue won stablecoins. The draft, titled the Act on the Innovation of the Digital Asset Industry and Protection of Users, was presented at a Virtual Asset Committee meeting chaired by FSC Chairman Lee Eog-weon. It would replace Korea’s two-track system, built on an anti-money-laundering law and a 2024 user protection act, with a single framework covering the industry, markets and users. Lee said the law would raise trust and transparency in Korea’s digital asset market and help draw new money into the industry. He said the government would do everything it can to see the bill fully debated in the National Assembly and enacted quickly. A 20% ownership cap for exchanges Under the bill, exchanges would become “digital asset platform operators,” a designation reserved for firms that hold separate licenses for dealing, brokerage and custody. The FSC modeled the ownership limit on the rules for alternative trading systems in the stock market. Major shareholders could own up to 20%, or up to 34% with FSC approval under a presidential decree. Shares above the limit would lose their voting rights. Existing exchanges would get three years after designation to comply, and small and midsize exchanges could get up to three more. The cap could reach some of Korea’s best-known exchanges. Mirae Asset Consulting owns 97.15% of Digital X, the exchange formerly known as Korbit, The Korea Herald reported . Naver Financial’s planned share-swap takeover of Dunamu, the operator of Upbit, would make the exchange a wholly owned subsidiary. The FSC declined to comment on specific companies, the paper said. “Ownership restrictions are necessary to strengthen exchanges’ public accountability and neutrality,” Yoo Young-jun, director general of the FSC’s Digital Financial Policy Bureau, said at a briefing, citing more than 10 million exchange accounts in Korea. The bill would also move trade execution, listing reviews and market surveillance from self-regulation to formal rules. Exchanges would need outside directors to make up a majority of their boards, plus audit committees and compliance officers. Coin offerings and won stablecoins Domestic initial coin offerings would be allowed as long as issuers file a white paper with the FSC before marketing tokens to the public. The release pointed to a platform company that sidestepped Korea’s ICO ban by setting up a foundation abroad, then sold its token through local exchanges. Exchanges would have to file and publish a report on each token they list. Stablecoins, called digital payment tokens in the bill, could only be issued by licensed firms with at least 5 billion won in capital. At first, the FSC plans to allow issuance only by

item.title: NYSC warns Bayelsa corps members against night movements, politicians
item.description: By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa The National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) in Bayelsa State has warned corps members deployed to the state to avoid late-night movements, compromising situations and unnecessary exposure to security risks. The State Coordinator, Mr Samuel Pepple, gave the warning on Tuesday during the low-key closing ceremony of the 2026 Batch C Stream II orientation course at the NYSC Permanent Orientation Camp, Boro Town, Kolokuma-Opokuma Local Government Area. Pepple urged the departing corps members to uphold discipline, remain security-conscious and demonstrate integrity as they proceed to their respective Places of Primary Assignment (PPAs). He advised them to embrace their postings, particularly those assigned to rural and riverine communities, assuring them of adequate security arrangements, decent accommodation and necessary safety equipment, including life jackets for those deployed to riverine areas. Emphasising personal safety, the coordinator urged the corps members to communicate their whereabouts to trusted persons and strictly adhere to security guidelines provided during the orientation course. On electoral responsibilities, Pepple warned them against political interference, inducements and other actions capable of compromising their integrity. He stressed that corps members must remain politically neutral and discharge any electoral responsibilities assigned to them with professionalism and patriotism. The state coordinator also encouraged them to integrate into their host communities, respect local cultures and traditions, and contribute meaningfully to the development of their areas of deployment. He noted that their services were particularly needed in rural and riverine communities, where access to essential services, especially education, remained limited. Reminding them that the orientation course was only the first phase of their service year, Pepple directed the corps members to report promptly to their PPAs after completing the necessary documentation. He also instructed them to obtain approval before embarking on any journey outside their places of primary assignment. Pepple expressed confidence in their ability to contribute meaningfully to national development, urging them to serve with courage, commitment and selflessness. He concluded by praying for their safety and a successful service year, wishing them journey mercies as they departed the camp for their respective places of primary assignment. item.title: 2027: Again, Atiku vows to restore subsidy; revive Ajaokuta steel mill
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Former Vice-President and African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar has renewed his pledge to restore fuel subsidy and promised to revive and complete the Ajaokuta Steel Mill if elected president in 2027. Atiku made the pledge at the ADC presidential campaign rally in Lokoja, Kogi State, on Tuesday, while restating his commitment to making life more affordable and creating jobs and prosperity through industrial investment. “Our leadership in the previous years have not met the aspirations of the people of Kogi State. I have already promised Nigerians that I will return subsidy. I want to let you know that I mean it. I am serious about it, and I am sincere about it. This will bring about affordability of your life,” Atiku said. He also pledged to revive and complete the Ajaokuta Steel Mill, saying foreign investment could fund the project without public spending. “Secondly, for me in particular, I want to promise you here today that I will revive and complete the Ajaokuta steel mill. This is very doable because we can bring in foreign investment to complete that without putting any money there. It is business…” he said. Atiku also promised to continue the Baro Port project by dredging the River Niger, saying the port could serve states beyond Kogi and create jobs and economic opportunities. “Again, let me assure you, people of Kogi State, we shall continue the project of the Baro Port by dredging the River Niger, so that Baro Port can also serve other states of Nigeria. So you can imagine Baro Port being an equivalent of Apapa Port. It would bring about tremendous job opportunities and prosperity for the people of Kogi State and the entire Northern states.” The former vice-president has previously described his subsidy plan as support for locally refined fuel to reduce production costs and make petrol more affordable, rather than a return to subsidising imported fuel. Vanguard reported that he said the policy was intended to reduce fuel and transport costs. item.title: Nigeria Urges UN To Clear 216 Outstanding Audit Queries
item.description: Nigeria’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Ambassador Jimoh Ibrahim, has urged the UN management to urgently resolve 216 outstanding audit queries, stressing the need for greater accountability, transparency and compliance with established financial rules and procedures. Ibrahim made the call during deliberations of the UN General Assembly’s Fifth Committee on reports of the United Nations Board of Auditors, where he expressed concern over the number of unresolved audit issues and called for improved performance by the organisation’s management. He acknowledged that 100 audit reports had been cleared but said the 216 outstanding reports remained a significant concern that required urgent attention. Although he recognised that some of the cases might have been overtaken by events, the Nigerian diplomat urged the UN management to improve its clearance rate, which currently stands at 55 per cent. Ibrahim also emphasised the importance of timely payment of assessed contributions by member states, insisting that payments should be made according to schedule and translated into tangible benefits. On financial reporting, he stressed that the accuracy and integrity of data were fundamental to the credibility of reports presented before member states. ﻿ He said all stakeholders had a collective responsibility to safeguard the integrity of information underpinning the UN’s financial reporting. The Nigerian envoy warned that continued explanations without corresponding compliance could leave the organisation trapped in an endless cycle of justifications. He, therefore, urged UN management to prioritise adherence to established financial rules and procedures as the most effective way to address recurring audit concerns. Ibrahim also commended the cooperation between information-gathering systems and audit teams, describing their coordination as essential to improving the quality and reliability of UN reports. Meanwhile, the Fifth Committee considered the Secretary-General’s report on the estimated use of the commitment authority for 2026 and the proposed 2027 subvention to the Extraordinary Chambers in the Courts of Cambodia. Speaking on behalf of the Group of 77 and China, Uruguay reaffirmed the group’s support for the proposed subvention, as well as its commitment to justice and national reconciliation. The Committee subsequently concluded its general discussion, with Canada’s representative, Sophia, expected to lead informal consultations to consolidate the observations and contributions of delegations. The Committee is scheduled to reconvene on November 30, 2026. The post Nigeria Urges UN To Clear 216 Outstanding Audit Queries appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: DOJ Moves to Forfeit $1.1 Billion in USDC Stolen in Binance Hack
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine DOJ Moves to Forfeit $1.1 Billion in USDC Stolen in Binance Hack The Justice Department filed a civil forfeiture complaint Monday to take ownership of more than $1.1 billion in USDC that North Korean hackers stole from Binance last month, tokens that Circle froze but says it cannot move. The complaint , filed in U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia, targets all USDC held at 36 addresses across 18 blockchains. The department said the U.S. has now helped freeze, seize or return more than $2.9 billion in crypto from multiple sources since the Oct. 29 theft. On Nov. 12, the department said it had court authority to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion, out of a joint government and industry freeze of more than $2.7 billion. A temporary restraining order issued that day was served on Circle the same day. Monday’s filing is the step that would let the government take title to the funds. Circle will mint replacement tokens Circle blocked access to the USDC on or about Oct. 29, the complaint says. But the stablecoin issuer told prosecutors it does not have the technical ability to transfer the tokens out of the blocklisted addresses, which remain under the hackers’ control. Instead, Circle has agreed to issue new USDC equal to the frozen amount and send it to the U.S. once a court enters a forfeiture order. The complaint calls those tokens “Substitute USDC.” Several of the addresses are smart contract and hot wallet addresses on Binance’s own platform. The hackers took them over in the attack and drained some, but not all, of the funds before Circle stepped in, prosecutors wrote. “It appears Binance no longer controlled them,” the complaint says. How the Binance hack worked The filing also lays out how investigators say the breach began. A Binance employee contacted by a purported recruiter agreed to a job interview and was told to download software that contained malware, which matches what the exchange said earlier this month. The infected device let the attackers plant an EIP-7702 injection. That feature, added to Ethereum in a 2025 upgrade, lets ordinary wallets temporarily act like smart contracts. Prosecutors said the hackers used it to take control of Binance’s hot wallets and route funds to a “sweeper” contract that moved them out as soon as they arrived. The first large transfer, about $780 million in USDC, left Binance on Ethereum at about 4:41 p.m. ET on Oct. 29, the complaint says. Another $43 million followed 18 minutes later. Investigators also traced AVAX that was split up, bridged and swapped until it became about $1.56 million in USDC. U.S. agencies attribute the theft to North Korean military hackers known as the Lazarus Group, or APT38. Investigators said some wallets that collected Binance funds also received money from the roughly $387 million Bitget hack in September, which the exchange’s CEO tied to North Korea. The complaint also lists earlier heists it attributes to the group, including about $308

This recognition encourages me to keep striving for excellence.” The runner-up, Opeyemi Sanusi Modinat, praised the company’s collaborative approach. “Our partnership has given us opportunities to grow, expand our market presence and serve more customers. item.title: Claude Ship puts AI at the helm of pull request approvals
item.description: Anthropic has introduced Claude Ship to review, fix, and approve pull requests (PRs), offering more AI automation to help teams handle the output of AI coding tools. Claude Ship combines the generally available Code Review service with two new agents in beta: PR Steward and Claude Approvals. It is available to Claude Team and Enterprise customers using GitHub repositories. Anthropic said : "On the Claude Code team, Claude writes most of our code, and we wanted everything after the PR to move that fast too." Its stated goal is to "ship code as fast as teams write it." One consequence of the AI coding revolution is the sheer amount of agent output, which requires review and approval before going live. Claude Ship is one way to address that by automating more of the workflow. PR Steward works through failing continuous integration (CI) checks, merge conflicts, and review feedback. Claude Approvals can actually approve a PR, something that might rattle the nerves of some engineers. Claude Approvals applies an approval policy, written by the team as a file in the repository. "Claude can approve routine changes on its own if the policy allows it, or can require deeper human sign-off for certain scenarios," Anthropic said. The company advised caution: "For most customers, we recommend enabling this first in observe-only mode to build confidence before configuring branch protection to require Claude Approvals' green light." While developers can try Claude Ship on their own pull requests (depending on their permissions and the repository's branch rules) with a /ship command in Claude Code, administrators can set up the rules on a repository-by-repository basis. "Claude Approvals starts when a connected repository has a policy file on its default branch, and an admin can turn it off," Anthropic said. "Teams set the pace. They can start with one repository, choose a review level and when reviews run, set a monthly spend limit, and run their approval policy in observe mode until they trust it." The extra automation also brings extra charges. Usage is token-based, and even observe-only approval policies can incur costs if they invoke classifiers or Code Review. Anthropic also includes the familiar disclaimer: "Claude Ship uses AI and may miss bugs, security vulnerabilities, or other issues." The Register spoke to an engineer who works for a company that uses Claude. They were a little cynical about the whole thing, saying: "It just seems like a glorification of what I already use Claude on – git merge or git rebase. "Our golden rule so far with Git is to limit Claude to read operations there; this layer of separation still lets devs stay in control and allows them a judgment of the AI changes – what to keep, tweak, or commit. "If that's offloaded to Claude and it has Git history-rewrite access, the devs will lose that overview and judgment opportunity." How much authority Claude receives depends on the organization's configuration. Approval is not the same as

item.title: Inside the 2026 WISCAR Mentoring Walk
item.description: Mentors, mentees, professionals and members of the public gathered at Eko Atlantic, Lagos, on Saturday, November 14, 2026, for the annual Women in Successful Careers (WISCAR) Mentoring Walk . Led by WISCAR Founder and Chairperson, Amina Oyagbola , the walk forms part of the lead-up to the organisation’s 18th Annual Leadership and Mentoring Conference. Participants were paired up for the walk along the Eko Atlantic, each with someone they had not met before. At the end of the route, they switched to new mentor-mentee partners for a short mentoring session, which gave everyone two fresh conversations in one morning. Back at the meeting point, participants shared what they had learnt from their partners, from career advice to personal lessons. Nutritionist Sherese Ijewere then led a session on healthy eating and answered questions on everyday food choices. Coach Bobbie Tee of Happy Heart Fitness, closed the morning with a Zumba session. Next stop: the conference The walk sets the stage for WISCAR’s 18th Annual Leadership and Mentoring Conference , themed “ Courage in Action: Shaping Policies and Structures for Inclusive Progress. ” The conference takes place on Saturday, November 28, 2026, at the Civic Centre, Lagos. Highlights include: A keynote from Dr Ndidi Nwuneli , former President and CEO of the ONE Campaign and Founder of LEAP Africa, who will also receive this year’s Distinguished WISCAR Award. Speakers including Badejo-Okusanya , SAN, President of the Nigerian Bar Association, and Mallam Ahmed Ladan Gobir, President of the Chartered Institute of Personnel Management (CIPM) The launch of WISCAR’s CIPM-endorsed Corporate Mentoring Playbook The graduation of Cohort 2 of the Women in Law Mentoring Programme Register now at https://wiscar.ng/almc . item.title: NASS Approves Tinubu’s $20.5bn, €1.45bn Supplementary External Borrowing Plan
item.description: The National Assembly has approved President Bola Tinubu’s request for a supplementary external borrowing plan of $20.517 billion and €1.45 billion for 2026 and 2027. The Senate approved the request on Tuesday following consideration of the recommendations of its Committee on Local and Foreign Loans. The approval came after the House of Representatives also endorsed the President’s borrowing plan. This file photo shows the red chamber of the Nigerian Senate. The proposed borrowing was calculated at an exchange rate of ₦1,400 to the dollar. Earlier on Tuesday, President Tinubu wrote to the Senate, seeking approval for a revised 2026 budget that reduces the previously approved expenditure by more than ₦3 trillion. The proposal, titled ‘Transmission of FGN 2026 Appropriation Repeal and Re-enactment Bill and Revised 2026 Federal Government Fiscal Framework’, was presented during plenary by Senate President Godswill Akpabio. House of Reps. (Photo by Facebook/House of Representatives, Federal Republic of Nigeria) Akpabio subsequently referred the correspondence to the Senate Committee on Rules and Business for legislative consideration. Under the revised fiscal framework, aggregate expenditure is projected at ₦65.176 trillion, down from the ₦68.323 trillion earlier approved by the National Assembly. Projected Federal Government revenue, including receipts from government-owned enterprises, stands at ₦33.720 trillion, while capital expenditure is pegged at ₦26.232 trillion. President Bola Tinubu signed into law the Appropriation (Amendment) (No.4) Bill, 2025, on September 30, 2026. Despite the reduction in overall expenditure, the fiscal deficit remains unchanged at ₦31.457 trillion, representing 5.64 per cent of the country’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP). The proposed new borrowing of ₦29.218 trillion also remains unchanged. This comprises ₦18.428 trillion in domestic borrowing and ₦10.790 trillion in external borrowing. Tinubu explained that the proposed $7.7 billion external loan, estimated at ₦10.368 trillion, would finance an existing foreign borrowing provision and would not increase the overall borrowing limit. According to the President, the adjustments are intended to prioritise existing commitments, strengthen the credibility of the budget and improve capital budget implementation while maintaining fiscal discipline. The development comes amid expectations that Tinubu will present the 2027 budget to the National Assembly before the end of December. item.title: Relai Launches Stacks, Letting Bitcoin Savers Split Plans by Goal
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Relai Launches Stacks, Letting Bitcoin Savers Split Plans by Goal Swiss bitcoin app Relai launched Stacks on Tuesday, a feature that lets users run several recurring bitcoin savings plans side by side, one for each goal, such as a house, a wedding or a child’s first car. Stacks is live for all Relai users in Switzerland and the European Union. Each Stack carries its own amount and schedule, and users can change either at any time without starting over, the company said. A savings plan is Relai’s version of dollar-cost averaging: buying a fixed amount of bitcoin on a set schedule, weekly or monthly, regardless of price. Savers use it to avoid timing the market. Since September, Relai users have been able to change the amount and buy date of an active plan. Stacks applies that to several goals at once, so a saver can put more toward a house one month, slow down a car fund the next and leave an emergency reserve untouched. In practice, Stacks is an organizing layer, not a new account. Relai’s help pages describe each Stack as a separate pot with its own bitcoin address inside the same wallet. Users get up to five custom Stacks plus a main balance, and moving bitcoin between them takes a regular on-chain transaction with a network fee. Self-custody cuts both ways Relai is self-custodial, meaning it does not hold customers’ bitcoin. The coins in every Stack sit in a wallet controlled by a 12-word recovery phrase, or seed phrase, that only the user has. All Stacks share that one phrase, and restoring the wallet with it brings every Stack back. The trade-off is responsibility. A saver who loses the phrase and the phone has no password reset and no support desk that can recover the coins. Anyone who gets the phrase can take them, which is why attackers have gone as far as tampering with hardware wallets to capture it. “Everyone saves for something. A home, their kids, the freedom to stop working one day,” said Julian Liniger, Relai’s co-founder and CEO. “With Stacks, you can save for each of those goals in Bitcoin, at your own pace.” How Relai is regulated In the EU, Relai’s French unit is authorized by France’s financial markets regulator, the AMF, as a crypto-asset service provider under MiCA, the bloc’s Markets in Crypto-Assets regulation . Relai secured that license in October 2025, and under MiCA a firm licensed in one member state can “passport” its services across the bloc. Swiss and Liechtenstein customers are served by Relai AG, which is affiliated with VQF , a self-regulatory organization recognized by Swiss regulator FINMA under the country’s anti-money laundering law. Goal-based saving in bitcoin also carries price risk that a bank savings account does not. Bitcoin traded near $60,000 on Tuesday, more than 50% below its record above $126,000 set in October 2025, after falling below $60,000 last week. item.title: Bitcoin Price Slips to $60,000 as November ETF Outflows Hit Record
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Slips to $60,000 as November ETF Outflows Hit Record The bitcoin price slipped back to near $60,000 early Tuesday, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data, as the Nvidia-fueled rally in stocks cooled and spot bitcoin ETFs posted another heavy day of outflows. Bitcoin faded to near $61,100 on Monday afternoon after spiking as high as $64,500 on Jensen Huang’s return as Nvidia CEO. The slide continued overnight. Bitcoin fell below $60,000 and touched about $59,400 before edging back to the $60,000 line ahead of the U.S. open. The bitcoin price is now down about 7% from Monday’s high, and it remains less than $5,000 above last week’s two-year low near $55,100. ETF outflows set a monthly record Monday’s ETF figure was the number traders were watching, and it came back negative. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs shed about $569.7 million on Monday. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) accounted for $509.3 million of that, while Fidelity’s FBTC was the only fund to take in money, adding $13.3 million. It was the fifth straight day of outflows. November’s withdrawals now total about $4.71 billion , topping June’s $4.5 billion record for the worst month since the funds launched in January 2024. Adam Haeems, head of asset management at Tesseract Group, had called Monday’s flow figure “the first real test of this bounce.” The pattern he flagged, with bitcoin falling during U.S. hours in step with ETF outflows, held again on Monday, and the bitcoin price has given back almost all of Monday’s gains. Stocks cool and the Fed stays hawkish Wall Street is also giving back some ground. Dow futures fell 0.5% , S&P 500 futures declined 1% and Nasdaq-100 futures dropped 2% early Tuesday. Nvidia (NVDA) slid about 5% in premarket trading after closing up 31.5% at $165.05 on Monday. Monday’s rally was the strongest day for both the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq since April 2025. The S&P 500 gained 4.7% and the Nasdaq Composite closed 6.5% higher , even as bitcoin failed to hold its own spike. “With Jensen’s return, it assures people massively,” Chris Beauchamp, chief market analyst at IG Group, told Reuters . “But it then opens up a whole list of questions that may not be answered very quickly.” Rates remain a headwind for the bitcoin price. New York Fed President John Williams said Monday that “there is still work to do” to bring inflation back to the Fed’s 2% target. Markets are fully pricing in a quarter-point hike from the current 3.75% to 4% range when the Fed meets Dec. 8-9. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has pushed back on a bigger hike , but traders still see about a 5% chance of a half-point move. The dollar index is hovering just below a 20-month high, and Wednesday’s PCE inflation report is the last major data point before the December decision. item.title: FCC proposes 'tit-for-tat' restrictions on foreign satellite operators
item.description: The US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) will vote in December on proposals [PDF] that would restrict foreign satellite operators in the same way their home countries restrict US providers. The telecoms regulator says the move is to "ensure reciprocity and fair dealing" in the rules governing satellite operators. The main aim appears to be hitting back at European efforts to build up the region's own space communications industries. According to the FCC, the US has so far welcomed satellite systems licensed abroad on a level playing field, but that regulators elsewhere have begun holding US systems to different rules than they apply to their own domestic suppliers. "This has operated to the disadvantage of American satellite providers that are or may be burdened with regulatory and spectrum limitations that their competitors in foreign nations simply do not face," said FCC chairman Brendan Carr. The FCC has singled out the EU's Digital Networks Act , which proposes harmonized connectivity rules across the bloc. A separate proposal would overhaul authorization for mobile satellite services (MSS) in the 2 GHz band after existing rights expire in May 2027. Earlier this year, the FCC laid out some of its concerns, saying that EU-wide authorization of satellite spectrum would replace the national licensing by member states "with which US satellite operators have become accustomed," and could require wholesale relicensing of any US systems operating in Europe. "The FCC voting on foreign satellite companies is consistent with the Digital Networks Act, but is more of a response to the EU's decisions on how it plans to allocate the EU-wide 2 GHz spectrum," CCS Insight analyst Joe Gardiner told The Register . "The EU outlined in its proposal that, for two-thirds of the spectrum, only operators based in the EU with EU ownership and aligned with the EU's strategic goals will be considered for the spectrum. "This has locked out companies like SpaceX and Amazon Leo from attaining access to spectrum that is highly valuable for satellite direct-to-device services. The US government is looking to retaliate, to support the US constellations that would have attempted to win this EU-wide spectrum." Following an initial consultation in March, the FCC will vote in December on opening a rulemaking to reconsider how foreign-licensed satellite operators gain access to the US market. "It is time for this regulatory asymmetry to end," Carr said, adding that the FCC now proposes to mirror any regulations that foreign nations apply to American satellite providers. "If there are limits or restrictions on American providers operating abroad, then the notice proposes to apply those or similar regulatory restraints to satellite providers from those countries that are operating here." item.title: Peter Obi Lacks Competence To Lead Nigeria, Tinubu 100% Better — Abure
item.description: Former National Chairman of the Labour Party, Julius Abure, has said the party’s former presidential candidate, Peter Obi, lacks the character and competence to lead Nigeria, insisting that President Bola Tinubu is “100 per cent better”. Abure said he would not support Obi’s presidential ambition in the 2027 general election, citing his experience working with the former Anambra State governor and the internal crisis that fractured the Labour Party. He made the remarks during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today , where he explained why he considered Tinubu a better choice among the leading contenders for the presidency. Abure was a key ally of Obi during the 2023 presidential campaign and campaigned extensively for him. However, Obi subsequently left the Labour Party following a protracted leadership crisis. He blamed Obi’s caretaker committee decision for deepening the Labour Party’s crisis, driving elected officials away and raising questions about his leadership. “If indeed Obi was a good leader, why did they not follow Peter Obi? Peter Obi doesn’t have the character and competence to lead the country; we are sorry to say. Given my experience, I now know better,” he said. Peter Obi and Julius Abure appear in court for the presidential election petitions tribunal on Friday, June 2, 2023 Asked whether his decision to campaign extensively for Obi in 2023 had been a mistake, Abure admitted that it might have been. “Yes, it may have been an error because I now know better. Experience, they say, is the best teacher. Now I have experienced working with Peter Obi and that he is unstable, unreliable, a pretender who cannot be trusted because of the way he treated the leadership of the party,” he said. ﻿ Asked whether he still considered Obi “a saint,” Abure declared his support for Tinubu, describing the president as a more suitable candidate. “President Bola Tinubu is 100 per cent better. Today, we have the right to support whatever candidate we want. Obviously, Peter Obi is out of the question for us to support, given our experiences with him. We made a critical analysis of all the candidates: Tinubu, Atiku and Obi. “We feel Tinubu is the best candidate for us to support, given his trajectory so far in office and his ability to resolve conflicts compared to Peter Obi. The stage we are in now requires someone who can bring people together because the country is more divided than ever before. We need a bridge-builder who can unite people, and I do not believe Peter Obi has that capacity at this critical time in our history,” he said. He, however, dismissed allegations that he was responsible for Obi’s departure from the Labour Party, describing such claims as a “clear misconception”. Nigeria Democratic Congress presidential candidate Peter Obi Iin Niger state. item.title: Amazon says hackers' AI agents found and exploited 0-day with little human input
item.description: Amazon said AI agents recently found and exploited a zero-day vulnerability with no human oversight beyond a simple instruction to get root access on an East Asian university server. The agents were running on Cairn, an open source AI penetration-testing framework. The hackers, who provided prompts in simplified Chinese and configured the model to the Chinese Standard Time zone, gave the agents a list of IP addresses and the goal: “obtain shell access.” In short order, the agents discovered a zero-day in an open source medical imaging AI application running on one of the target servers. The agents then exploited the vulnerability and gained full control of the system. “These findings show that agentic offensive operations are already happening, and defenders should prepare for the speed and persistence these tools enable,” Amazon said . Read full article Comments

item.title: CrowdStrike splashes $44B on Zscaler, customers brace for the bill
item.description: CrowdStrike has agreed to buy Zscaler for $43.9 billion in what would be the biggest cybersecurity acquisition on record, and customers are already bracing for pricier renewals. The all-stock deal, announced on Monday , will see Zscaler shareholders receive 1.135 CrowdStrike shares for every share they own, representing a 34 percent premium on Friday's closing price. The transaction dwarfs even Google's $32 billion acquisition of cloud security upstart Wiz . Buying Zscaler gives CrowdStrike a sizeable foothold in the network security market, where it will be going up against the likes of Palo Alto Networks and Fortinet. The plan is to combine Falcon's endpoint protection capabilities with Zscaler's zero-trust network security technology, giving customers a single platform for securing devices and the connections between them. Naturally, there's an AI angle to the biggest cyber deal in history. CrowdStrike reckons owning both technologies will allow it to keep tabs on what AI agents are doing on corporate devices, where they're connecting, and what data they're getting their hands on. CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz described the proposed combination as "cybersecurity’s operating system." The acquisition also gives CrowdStrike's salespeople plenty to get excited about. Around 8,000 Zscaler customers don't currently buy CrowdStrike's wares, and the companies already have more than 2,000 customers in common. CrowdStrike reckons it can boost its annualized revenue by around $1 billion within 30 months of closing the deal by selling more products to the two companies' existing customers. Some of those customers, however, don't sound particularly keen on being cross-sold to. Over on Reddit's r/sysadmin subreddit, news of the purchase was met with a familiar set of concerns from IT professionals who've lived through big-ticket enterprise software acquisitions before. "As a zscaler customer, this does worry me. Cost increase, forced move to Falcon, integration issues, etc," wrote one sysadmin. Another, whose organization already uses both vendors' products, added: "I think they're both great products but I imagine they'll jack up the price for our next renewal. Fun." CrowdStrike intends to make Zscaler's products available through its Falcon Flex licensing scheme, which allows customers to commit to a certain level of spending and pick and choose the products they deploy. Monday's acquisition announcement didn't spell out what the deal would mean for customers who want to continue using Zscaler alongside a rival endpoint security product. Others raised concerns about the fate of Red Canary, the managed detection and response specialist snapped up by Zscaler in August 2025. CrowdStrike already operates a competing service in Falcon Complete. There may also be some nervous employees at both companies. item.title: One terminal command gave my forgotten Android device a desk job
item.description: My kitchen junk drawer used to hold takeout menus and coupons, but it has since become a storage spot for old tablets or phones. Like me, you probably have a few devices lying around that are perfectly functional but don't meet your daily driving needs. It's tucked out of view, living out its life in a drawer until being erased and donated after someone asks why you're holding onto outdated, unused devices. Thankfully, PhoneBox has a solution. You weren't hoarding old tech; you were waiting for the proper use. The PhoneBox home screen displays useful stats and what's currently playing in your browser. Credit: Nick Indge I had an old AllDoCube iPlay 50 mini Pro 8.4-inch tablet that seemed like the perfect candidate. I bought the tablet second-hand as a possible big-screen gaming and emulation tablet to use with a telescopic control deck, but I quickly found I vastly preferred just using a dedicated device. Since that realization, this decent little unit has lived its life in "the drawer." Launch applications on your PC from the connected Android device. Credit: Nick Indge Installation is a doddle Getting PhoneBox up and running on my tablet and PC couldn't have been simpler. After making sure that the Android tablet was in developer mode, the process was as easy as plugging the tablet in to my PC via USB and executing a single copied command in my Linux terminal. The script downloaded the PhoneBox 0.9.29 software for my PC, verified the downloaded checksum against the release, and walked me through a few quick Y/N installation questions. The script offers to create a systemd user service, so the desktop agent launches after initial login, and even asks if you'd like it to install the PhoneBox APK to your connected Android device.
